# Group 3 — Map / Page Identity and Navigation Survey

Corpus: `/mnt/c/Users/manci/PROJECTS/concur-corpus/CONCUR_INVOICE`, SAP version 2026_08, Professional Edition, crawled 2026-08-29.
Scope: the two Group 3 pages only — **Purchase Order Matching Rules** and **Purchase Order Configuration**.
Every quote below was verified with `grep -F -c` against its cited file before being written down (34/34 passed, 0 failures).

---

## 1. Purchase Order Matching Rules

**Verdict: it is a real admin page. Confirmed, not assumed.**
Two independent pieces of evidence establish page-hood rather than mere feature-hood:
`access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md` says the click produces a page —
"Click Purchase Order Matching Rules (left menu). The Purchase Order Matching Rules page appears." —
and `step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md` independently refers to
"On the Purchase Order Matching Rules page, select the rule set, and then click Edit."
Two different guide topics, both using the word *page*, both anchored to the same label.

### 1.1 Documented click paths (five distinct, six quotes)

| # | navPath | File | Quote |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Administration › Invoice › Purchase Order Matching Rules | admin `access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md` | `Click Purchase Order Matching Rules (left menu). The Purchase Order Matching Rules page appears.` |
| 2 | Administration › Invoice (first two segments only) | admin `access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md` | `1.  Click Administration > Invoice.` |
| 3 | Administration › Invoice › Purchase Order Matching Rules | admin `configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md` | `Click Administration > Invoice > Purchase Order Matching Rules (left menu).` |
| 4 | Administration › Invoice › Purchase Order Matching Rules | admin `purchase-order-matching-rules-8b357dbb.md` (legacy twin) | `Admins create these rules by going to Administration > Invoice > Purchase Order Matching Rules.` |
| 5 | Administration › Invoice › Purchase Order Matching Rules | admin `purchase-order-matching-rules-new-experience-6c8fb80f.md` (New Experience twin) | same sentence, different file — an independent attestation, not a duplicate |
| 6 | Administration › Invoice › Purchase Order Matching Rules | admin `overview-8b37481c.md` | NBSP-separated variant (see 1.2) |

The **canonical access topic (`8407c500`) is the only two-step form**: step 1 `Click Administration > Invoice.`, step 2
`Click Purchase Order Matching Rules (left menu).` Everything else is the collapsed one-line form.

### 1.2 TEXT TRAP — `overview-8b37481c.md` uses NON-BREAKING SPACES as the menu separator

That file writes the path with **no `>` characters at all** and U+00A0 between segments:
`it is configured by going to \xa0\xa0Administration\xa0\xa0Invoice\xa0\xa0Purchase Order Matching Rules.`
Rendered, that looks like `Administration  Invoice  Purchase Order Matching Rules`. Any grep or extractor
keyed on `Administration > Invoice` **misses this file entirely** — it is a third nav attestation invisible to the
obvious search. **Emission decision:** the NBSP-bearing string *does* pass `grep -F` (verified), but a single U+00A0 normalised
anywhere in JSON transport would fail the deterministic validator and take the build down with it. So the emitted
sourceQuote for this attestation is the ASCII-only lead-in
`Receipt confirmation is part of the PO Matching feature set. As such, it is configured by going to`
and the NBSP variant is recorded here in prose instead. The attestation is preserved; the build risk is not taken.

### 1.3 The "Invoice Processing Admin" middle node is UNATTESTED for this page

Corpus-wide, `Invoice Processing Admin` is documented as the middle nav node for Email Reminders, Exceptions,
Group Configurations, Workflows, Expense Types, Policies, Invoice Settings, Change Log, Forms and Fields,
Routing Configuration, Company Locations, and Peppol Configuration. **It is never written in front of
Purchase Order Matching Rules.** All five documented paths go straight Administration › Invoice › Purchase Order
Matching Rules. Treat the middle segment as **UNATTESTED, not absent** — a driver should be prepared to try both.

Note also that this page is the **only PO label in the corpus ever written with "(left menu)"** — it appears in
`8407c500` and in `configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md`, and nowhere else on any PO surface.

### 1.4 Aliases (what the corpus actually calls it)

| Alias | Attested? | Where / caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase Order Matching Rules | canonical | page name, menu label, topic titles |
| Purchase Order Matching Set | **yes, as an alias for the same surface** | `edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md`: `In Purchase Order Matching Set, select the rule set row under Rule Set Name.` and `step-3-...-64eb1c47.md`: `In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.` |
| Purchase Order Matching Rules (New Experience) | yes | title of `6c8fb80f` |
| PO matching rules / matching rule set | yes, lowercase prose only | never used as a menu label |
| Match Rules | yes, as a **concept** in tools-guides | `match-rules-and-match-status-8cc2c56b.md`, `when-are-match-rules-run-f835a01e.md` — never a click target |
| PO Matching Rules (title case) | **NOT attested as a page label** | see the trap below |

**TRAP — "PO Matching Ruleset" is a FIELD ON THE ALREADY-BUILT POLICIES PAGE, NOT AN ALIAS FOR THIS PAGE.**
`access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md`: "You select a rule set using the PO Matching Ruleset option in
Policies." It also appears in `components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md`, `create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md`,
`purchase-order-policy-fields-4aa0ac1b.md`, and `policies-the-purchase-order-policy-new-experience-5a1ba7ef.md`.
Do not re-home it. The near-miss is real: the string that most looks like a short alias for this page is in fact
a control on someone else's page.

### 1.5 Recon findings — CONFIRMED against the corpus

**(a) "Purchase Order Matching Set" is an alias, not a second page — CONFIRMED, and the corpus is internally sloppy
about it.** `edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md` puts the admin *inside* the surface at step 1
(`In Purchase Order Matching Set, select the rule set row under Rule Set Name.`) and then at step 2 says
`Click Edit to open Purchase Order Matching Set.` You cannot be in a thing and then open it. The only reading that
survives is that "Purchase Order Matching Set" is a loose second name for the same rule-set surface, applied both to
the list and to the editor that opens over it. No click path anywhere reaches a "Purchase Order Matching Set" page.

**(b) "Purchase Order Policy" is not a page — CONFIRMED.** `grep` over both guide directories for
"Purchase Order Policy" intersected with click/nav language (`click`, `left menu`, `Administration`, `page appears`)
returns **zero lines**. It is a policy *type* on the already-built Policies page.

**(c) The Rules / Life to Date tabs and the Group Conditions, Select Confirmation Type and Exception Message dialogs
belong to this page — CONFIRMED.** None has its own path from Administration. Each is reached only from inside the
rule-set editor: `In Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions, configure the conditions` (step-4),
`Do this by clicking Edit Confirmation to open the Select Confirmation Type window` (step-5), and the Exception
Message editor `Exception Message: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by
selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save.` (configure-three-way-matching, twice). The Audit Rules precedent
holds: one page, several tabs.

**(d) A FIFTH dialog exists — the Exception Message editor.** The recon click tree omitted it. It is attested twice
in `configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md` and once in `step-2-...-dc296ae6.md`. A driver cannot set an exception
message without it. Recorded here so the field/dependency pass does not lose it.

### 1.6 CONTRADICTION — tab depth. Recorded, NOT reconciled.

Two irreconcilable readings of where the Rules and Life to Date tabs sit:

* **One level up, no Edit Rules step** — `step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md`:
  `In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.` The admin is on the rule-set surface and clicks the tab directly.
* **Two levels down, after Edit Rules** — `step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md`:
  `On the Purchase Order Matching Rules page, select the rule set, and then click Edit.` →
  `Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group).` →
  `Click the Life to Date tab, then select the check box next to the rule type to activate`.
  And `configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md`:
  `in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules. The Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window appears.` →
  `Click the Life to Date tab, and then select the Match against Received Quantity option.`

**Majority tree (2 topics to 1): Purchase Order Matching Rules → select rule set → Edit → select rule group →
Edit Rules → [Rules | Life to Date] tabs.** The step-3 shallow reading is the minority and is recorded as a
disagreement, not deleted. This matters for automation: the driver must probe for the tabs at both depths.

Related contradiction, already flagged by recon and confirmed here — **the Tolerance value list has two documented
readings**: `step-3-...-64eb1c47.md` line 45 `Choose one tolerance:` enumerates FOUR (None, Within (+/-), Custom,
Currency); `configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md` line 46 `in the Tolerance section, select None, Within, or
Custom, and then select Value or Percentage.` enumerates THREE. Both must be emitted by the field pass. Not my
node to build, but it is a page-level contradiction and belongs in this survey.

### 1.7 UI variant — "both", and I read both twins

`purchase-order-matching-rules-8b357dbb.md` (legacy title) and `purchase-order-matching-rules-new-experience-6c8fb80f.md`
were diffed line by line. The bodies are **byte-identical** except for the title/heading and one appended block.
The New Experience file contributes exactly one unique substantive procedure — `"Unlock" a Matching Rule Set From Its
In-Use Status` — plus restatements of Test and Change Match Rule Sets and Activate Exchange Rates that already exist
as their own topics (`test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md`, `activate-exchange-rates-for-matching-rule-sets-c51af31c.md`).
So: **uiVariant = both**, and the config surface does **not** differ between variants in anything the corpus documents.
Do not double-count a control because it appears in both twins.

### 1.8 Role gate

Three attestations, one role, spelled two ways:
* admin `required-roles-ec6fae13.md` — `Only the user with the Invoice Configuration Administrator role can access and configure the Purchase Order Matching Rules feature.`
* tools `required-roles-ef2c2901.md` — `Only the Invoice Configuration administrator can access and configure the Purchase Order Matching Rules feature.`
* admin `overview-8b35a33f.md` — `Only accessible by users with the Invoice Configuration Administrator role.`

The only variance is capitalisation (`Administrator` vs `administrator`). Same role. This is the cleanest role gate
in the Group 3 set — attested in **both** guide directories, which is exactly the cross-directory check that nearly
lost Vendor Search Admin.

### 1.9 CORPUS DEFECT — `create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md` is TRUNCATED

Its body ends with a bare line containing only `x`. It is the only file corpus-wide that does. Content was dropped in
the 2026-08-29 crawl. Anything taken from it must carry that caveat. It still yields the two rule TYPES (Life to Date,
Rules) intact before the cut, so it is usable — but it is not complete and must never be treated as an exhaustive list.

### 1.10 documentedBasis = **rich**

Justification: field-level documentation across multiple independent topics — a 6-row Life to Date selection table
(Gross Amount, Net Amount, Line Item Total, Line Item Quantity, Match against Received Quantity, Line Item Tax) in
step-2; a Level value list (Header, Vendor, Line Item, Line Item - Receipt) in step-3; two tolerance lists;
a 3-row confirmation-type table with default message text in step-5; Value/Percentage/Currency refinements;
Exception Message and Allow Submit/Approve controls; and a 6-value Match Status catalog in tools-guides
(`understand-the-match-status-assigned-to-an-invoice-52477c6b.md`). Forty-five files, ~64 KB of body text, and the
documentation names controls, not just concepts. `coverageGuess = good` — the one real hole is the truncated
`adb700f9`, and the material it would have carried is largely recoverable from the step topics.

## 2. Purchase Order Configuration

**Verdict: it is a real admin page. Confirmed — but on much thinner and structurally different evidence.**
Page-hood rests on two nav quotes that both name the label as a click target off Administration › Invoice. The corpus
calls it a **tool** and a **window**, never a "page" — unlike PO Matching Rules, no topic anywhere says
"the Purchase Order Configuration page appears".

### 2.1 Documented click paths (two distinct, from BOTH guide directories)

| # | navPath | File | Quote |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Administration › Invoice › Purchase Order Configuration | admin `use-the-purchase-order-configuration-tool-51009c8c.md` | `To view this tool, click Administration > Invoice > Purchase Order Configuration.` |
| 2 | Administration › Invoice › Purchase Order Configuration | tools `preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md` | `the Invoice Configuration administrator uses the Purchase Order Configuration tool (Administration > Invoice > Purchase Order Configuration).` |

Cross-directory corroboration of the click path is real and matters: path #2 lives in **tools-guides**, and an
admin-guides-only sweep would have found a single unattested-elsewhere nav line. Same near-miss shape as Vendor
Search Admin.

`Invoice Processing Admin` is again **UNATTESTED** as a middle node for this page — zero occurrences in front of
this label anywhere in the corpus, while the node is well documented for a dozen sibling pages on the same menu.
Same instruction to the driver: try both.

### 2.2 Aliases

| Alias | Attested? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase Order Configuration | canonical | menu label in both nav quotes |
| Purchase Order Configuration tool | yes | `use-the-purchase-order-configuration-tool-51009c8c.md`, `preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md` |
| Purchase Order Configuration window | yes, but only in a **release-history table** | `purchase-request-and-purchase-order-8b36ae07.md` line 209 — a revision-history row, weak; not cited as a source |
| PO Configuration | yes | tools `preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md`: `Administrators who configure purchase orders in PO Configuration` |
| PO configuration (lowercase) | yes | `purchase-order-configuration-is-group-aware-b603f04b.md`, tools `manage-images-03021850.md` |

### 2.3 THE LOAD-BEARING WARNING — the field roster file NAMES NEITHER THE PAGE NOR A PATH

`grep -c "Purchase Order Configuration" configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md` returns **ZERO**. Verified. The only
near-hit is line 89, lowercase and incidental: "The logo is group-aware in the same way as the purchase order
configuration...". That file carries **all twelve settings sections** and is essentially the whole page, and it binds
to this page by **GUIDE-SECTION ADJACENCY ALONE**.

Independent attestation by name exists for only **four of the twelve**:

| Section | Binding |
|---|---|
| Company Name Without Address | **independently attested by name** — `purchase-request-and-purchase-order-8b36ae07.md` line 209 names the field in the Purchase Order Configuration window |
| Company Branding Logo | **independently attested** — line 89 of the roster file itself ties the logo to "the purchase order configuration" and its group-awareness |
| Company Address | **independently attested** — `preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md`: "To change default text (Body text, address, Instructions, etc.) the Invoice Configuration administrator uses the Purchase Order Configuration tool" |
| Supporting Documents | **independently attested, cross-directory** — tools `manage-images-03021850.md`: `The PO configuration associated with a Group may also include supporting documents.` and `Administrators who configure purchase orders in PO Configuration` |
| PO Number Generation | ADJACENCY-ONLY |
| Message to Include on Transmitted Purchase Orders | ADJACENCY-ONLY |
| Default Email Subject When Transmitting Purchase Orders | ADJACENCY-ONLY |
| Default Email Message When Transmitting Purchase Orders | ADJACENCY-ONLY |
| Default Sender Email | ADJACENCY-ONLY |
| Fields to Appear on Purchase Orders | ADJACENCY-ONLY |
| Ship To Without Requestor Name | ADJACENCY-ONLY |
| Use Email as Bill-To | ADJACENCY-ONLY |

Every field node built for this page must state which of the two it is in its notes. **Adjacency is not attestation.**
The deterministic validator checks quotes against files; it cannot see a control bound to the wrong page.

### 2.4 Unenumerated list and SAP typo

"Fields to Appear on Purchase Orders" is an **unenumerated** field-selection list:
`The header and line time fields you select will appear on the purchase order.` — the selectable header and line-item
roster is never enumerated anywhere in the corpus. Mark it unenumerated; do not guess the members.
**SAP typo:** "line time fields" is written for "line item fields". Text trap for any extractor keyed on "line item".

### 2.5 No long catalog on this page

Measured on `configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md`: `grep -c "^| "` = 0, `grep -c "^-   "` = 0, `grep -c "<table"` = 0.
The twelve "sections" are **prose section headings**, not an enumeration. What makes the page tractable is that each
of the twelve carries a stated limit or constraint (9-character PO number, 3200-character message, 500-character
email subject, .png/.jpg/.gif at 55px × ≤200px × ≤100KB logo, `PurchaseOrder_DoNotReply@ConcurSolutions.com`
suffix that cannot be changed).

### 2.6 Group scope

`purchase-order-configuration-is-group-aware-b603f04b.md`: `Each PO configuration you create is based on the Group you
select before creating the configuration.` and `Groups with no PO configuration assigned use the Global Group
configuration by default.` Corroborated cross-directory by `manage-images-03021850.md`, which is also the **only**
statement anywhere of how admin-uploaded and user-uploaded PO attachments interact. Group selection is therefore a
**precondition** on this page, not a field — it gates what the other twelve write to.

### 2.7 UI variant — undifferentiated. Do NOT claim "new" or "both".

The corpus contains exactly five `*-new-experience-*` files: `end-user-experience-new-experience-85c2652b.md`,
`policies-the-purchase-order-policy-new-experience-5a1ba7ef.md`, `purchase-order-matching-rules-new-experience-6c8fb80f.md`,
`using-the-invoice-manager-page-new-experience-f83ba5fa.md`, `using-the-unassigned-invoice-page-new-experience-072e2f18.md`.
**None is PO Configuration.** No variant labelling exists for this page in either direction, so `undifferentiated`.

### 2.8 Two seeds correctly excluded — confirmed, and must not be re-added

* `purchase-order-processor-experience-8b507c54.md` is an **end-user processor** topic. It mentions "Purchase Order
  Configuration is Group-Aware" only as a pointer and refers the reader elsewhere for the tool. Not a field source.
* `purchase-order-setup-process-9f253ce7.md` never names this tool; it is a setup-flow stop list (it lists
  "Match Rules" as an ordering step). Evidence about ordering, not about fields.

### 2.9 Role gate

* admin `use-the-purchase-order-configuration-tool-51009c8c.md` — `The Purchase Order Configuration tool is available to the Invoice Configuration administrator for setting default information for purchase orders.`
* tools `preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md` — `the Invoice Configuration administrator uses the Purchase Order Configuration tool`

Same role as PO Matching Rules: **Invoice Configuration administrator**. Attested in both directories.

### 2.10 documentedBasis = **moderate**

Justification: real field-level documentation exists — twelve named settings, each with a stated limit or constraint,
plus group scope and role gate corroborated cross-directory. But the gaps are obvious and structural: eight of the
twelve bind to the page by adjacency only; the largest control ("Fields to Appear on Purchase Orders") is an
unenumerated list; the corpus never once calls it a page; and there is no catalog, no table, and no value enumeration
anywhere on the surface. That is textbook "some field-level documentation, gaps obvious" — not `rich`, and clearly not
`sparse`, because seven files and ~10 KB of body text do describe named controls with real constraints.
`coverageGuess = partial`, driven by the unenumerated field list and the adjacency-only binding.

1. **NBSP menu separators** in `overview-8b37481c.md` — a whole nav attestation invisible to `Administration > Invoice`.
2. **`PO Matching Ruleset` looks like an alias and is a foreign field.** Highest-risk confusion on this page.

   Group 3 nav path uses it.
7. **`create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md` is truncated** — body ends with a bare `x`.

## 0. HEADLINE FINDINGS (read before extracting)

1. **RAW `<table>` CENSUS IS A CLEAN NEGATIVE FOR BOTH PAGES.** Corpus-wide there are exactly **31** raw-HTML-table files in admin-guides and **1** in tools-guides (32 total, enumerated in §4). **Not one of them is a field/value source for either Group 3 page.** The two PO-adjacent ones are illustrative, not catalogs: `configure-forms-and-fields-for-purchase-order-copy-down-to-pr-f926eac7.md` (5 `<table>`, **5 `<tr>` total**, a pencils example — Forms and Fields territory, Group 5, already built) and `policies-the-purchase-order-policy-new-experience-5a1ba7ef.md` (5 `<table>`, **5 `<tr>` total** — Policies, Group 1, already built). Measured, not eyeballed. This closes the raw-table risk for this run.
2. **NEW CONTRADICTION — the "Unlock" procedure exists TWICE with TWO DIFFERENT CONTROL LABELS.** The brief's claim (5) — that `purchase-order-matching-rules-new-experience-6c8fb80f.md` contributes one unique procedure ("Unlock a Matching Rule Set From Its In-Use Status") — is **contradicted by the corpus**. That section also exists in full in `test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md`, and the two disagree on the control name:

   **Net effect: the New Experience twin contributes ZERO unique substantive procedures.** The instruction not to double-count the twins holds even harder than the brief states.
3. **NEW CROSS-DIRECTORY TWIN CONTRADICTION — Quantity Receipt ingestion routes.** Distinct `loio`s (so a genuine twin pair, not a gerund/imperative republish):

(both grep -F -c = 1 in the cited file). The already-built graph models 121 fields of fieldType 'button', so buttons are in scope for this schema and a Chromium driver needs each one addressably. NOT SPLIT HERE, and reported instead, because records created during Repair never face the adversarial refuter and three new page-bound records is exactly the mis-assignment class grep cannot catch. pages.verifyNotes: INPUTS AND ARITHMETIC. 21 judged candidates in (7 KEEP, 13 REPAIR, 1 pre-DROP). 16 records out, 5 in dropped[]. No record was created during Repair - every emitted name is an input canonicalName or one of that input's own variantSpellings. Every quote was pulled programmatically out of the three extraction JSONs (no retyping) and re-verified at assembly with grep -F -c against the cited file under ROOT: all 16 return exactly 1. No sourceFile carries the CONCUR_INVOICE/ prefix. No two records share a name, and none of the 16 names collides with any of the 437 existing field names in kg-invoice-config.json (checked programmatically; the near neighbours - field.policies.policy-name, field.group-configurations.group, field.expense-types.importPolicy - are all distinct strings and distinct controls). THE REFUTERS DISAGREED ON FIVE DUPLICATE PAIRS AND I HAD TO ADJUDICATE. For message-to-include, default-email-subject, default-email-message and default-sender-email, refuter 1 kept the Title-Case documented-label record (documentary fidelity) and refuter 2 kept the snake_case record (one naming family per page). Both agreed the loser's content must be folded into the survivor. I resolved every pair the same way: emit the snake_case spelling of the FULL documented label (a variantSpelling already present in the input), which is snake_case AND not an invented abbreviation. For default_sender_email I additionally dropped the '_prefix' suffix, because refuter 1's point is substantive rather than stylistic - the field is Default Sender Email and the prefix is what you type into it. In each pair I took the LONGER of the two verified quotes so the load-bearing detail sits inside the quote rather than only in notes, and merged both records' notes. Nothing in the losers' notes was discarded; the dropped[] entries name what was carried forward. REPAIRS ACTUALLY PERFORMED (9). (1) group_selector - the extractor asserted the group-aware topic 'never names the tool by its full title'; that is FALSE, grep -c 'Purchase Order Configuration' on that file = 3 (title, breadcrumb, H1), re-verified here, so the binding was upgraded from ADJACENCY-ONLY to INDEPENDENTLY ATTESTED BY NAME; fieldType 'dropdown' was demoted to 'unknown' because the widget is never stated and its very presence on this surface is unattested; and the missing boundary was added - the corpus states only that the Group is chosen BEFORE the configuration is created and never says WHERE, so the selector's LOCATION is unattested and the driver must be prepared for it to sit outside this tool. (2) po_number_prefix - renamed off Title Case into the po_number_* family, label deliberately left as the source's lowercase 'prefix' because Title Case is NOT an attested on-screen label; emitted over the procedures lens' withholding, per both refuters. (3) po_number_postfix - rebuilt on the tables-lens variant (refuter 1's named merge base) so the now-stale sentence claiming no Prefix control was emitted is struck. (4) supporting_documents - fieldType repaired from 'table' (zero documentary basis; no table, grid, or list widget is described anywhere) to 'unknown'. (5) policy - renamed to lowercase and given the explicit cross-page disambiguation refuter 2 required. (6-9) the four merged duplicate pairs above. Zero repair items were abandoned; nothing had to be moved to dropped[] for want of grounding. PAGE-BINDING DISCIPLINE, THE DEFECT THE VALIDATOR CANNOT SEE. grep -c 'Purchase Order Configuration' on the roster file configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md = 0, re-verified at assembly: the file carrying nearly every control on this page names neither the page nor a nav path. Every one of the 16 records states in notes whether its page binding is INDEPENDENTLY ATTESTED BY NAME or ADJACENCY-ONLY. FIVE are attested by name - company_address (preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md, tools-guides), supporting_documents (manage-images-03021850.md, tools-guides), company_branding_logo and company_name_without_address (purchase-request-and-purchase-order-8b36ae07.md), and group_selector (its own topic title, per the repair above). The other ELEVEN are adjacency-only. Adjacency is not attestation and is not presented as such anywhere in this roster. VALUE SET WIRING - ACTION REQUIRED AT MERGE, IT IS NOT FIXABLE FROM INSIDE THIS ROSTER SHAPE. Both refuters flagged it under rule 7. The page's ONLY valueSetCandidate (the closed enumeration .png / .jpg / .gif, from 'You can upload a .png, .jpg, or .gif file.') lives in extract-purchase-order-configuration-tables.json with appliesToField 'Company Branding Logo' - a UI LABEL and the tables lens' field name. The surviving field NAME is company_branding_logo. Unless the merge re-points appliesToField (and appliesToRef.field) to company_branding_logo, this page's only value set lands UNWIRED - the same failure that stranded 17 sets in an earlier run. The instruction is repeated inside that field's notes so it cannot be lost. TWO EXISTING GRAPH EDGES TO RESOLVE, NOT DUPLICATE. dep.g1.057 ('precedes') and dep.g1.058 ('triggers', the Global Group fallback) already run from field.group-configurations.group to an unresolved targetRef {page: 'Purchase Order Configuration', field: 'PO Configuration'}, quoting the same two group-aware sentences group_selector is built from; building this page should RESOLVE them rather than emit parallel dependencies. dep.g5g5.027 already carries the Use Email as Bill-To prerequisite sourceQuote verbatim; link, do not duplicate. NAME RECOMMENDATION I DECLINED TO ACT ON, REPORTED INSTEAD. Refuter 2 asked that group_selector be renamed so it does not read as an attested picker (suggesting group_scope_precondition). I left the name as the input canonicalName because the roster's hard constraint forbids emitting a name that is not in the KEEP or REPAIR lists, and handled the substance in notes instead - the record now says plainly that no Group control is documented on this tool and that this is a scope precondition, not an attested widget. If the graph owner wants the rename, it is a safe one-line change at merge. NO INVENTED VALUES. All 16 records carry validValues: []. The three checkbox-shaped toggles (ship_to_without_requestor_name, company_name_without_address, use_email_as_bill_to) explicitly refuse to manufacture the disabled half of a pair the corpus describes one side of. fields_to_appear_on_purchase_orders stays UNENUMERATED and was not back-filled from the Forms and Fields copy-down roster (a raw <table> in configure-forms-and-fields-for-purchase-order-copy-down-to-pr-f926eac7.md) nor from the three named header fields on this page. The PO email subject tokens stay unenumerated and the Email Message Helper token table from email-message-replacement-tokens-c9cc4af4.md was NOT imported (it is scoped to reminder email subjects and bodies on a different surface). SAP's typo 'line time fields' for 'line item fields' is preserved verbatim inside the quote and flagged as a text trap. fromRawHtmlTable IS false ON ALL 16 AND THAT IS CORRECT: every cited file returns grep -c '<table' = 0 and the indentation-tolerant grep -cP '^\s*\|' = 0. There is no long catalog on this page; the recon's earlier longCatalogs:1 score was retracted on measurement and I did not resurrect it. uiVariant 'undifferentiated' on every record - no *-new-experience-* file is PO Configuration. mustReadSkipped: NONE; both refuters read all five must-read files in full and I re-verified the two load-bearing greps (page name = 0 in the roster file, = 3 in the group-aware file) myself rather than trusting the report. COVERAGE IS 'partial', NOT 'good'. Real field-level documentation exists - sixteen controls, nearly all carrying a stated limit or constraint (9-character PO number, 3200-character message, 500-character subject, .png/.jpg/.gif logo at 55px high / <=200px long / <=100KB and one per invoice group, a fixed _DoNotReply@ConcurSolutions.com suffix) - but the gaps are structural, not incidental: eleven of sixteen bind to this page by guide-section adjacency alone, the page's largest control is an unenumerated field list, there is no catalog or value enumeration anywhere on the surface, the corpus never states whether the twelve prose sections correspond to twelve UI sections, and it never places a Group selector on this tool at all. Six documented action controls (Upload/View/Remove on the logo and on supporting documents) are described in notes rather than emitted as fields - see splitsProposed. That is an honest 'partial', and I did not pad it toward 'good'.

pages.identityNotes: PAGE-HOOD CONFIRMED, but on structurally weaker evidence than PO Matching Rules. Two distinct click paths, one from EACH guide directory - the tools-guides path (preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md) is genuine cross-directory corroboration and an admin-guides-only sweep would have left the page resting on a single line. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: the corpus calls this a 'tool' and a 'window' and NEVER a 'page' - no topic anywhere says 'the Purchase Order Configuration page appears'. It is nonetheless a real admin surface reached by clicking off Administration > Invoice. MIDDLE NAV NODE 'Invoice Processing Admin' is UNATTESTED here too - zero occurrences in front of this label anywhere in the corpus, while it is documented for a dozen sibling pages on the same menu; the driver must be prepared to try both. THE LOAD-BEARING DEFECT: configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md carries ALL TWELVE settings sections and is essentially the whole page, yet grep -c "Purchase Order Configuration" on it returns ZERO (verified). It names neither the page nor a nav path. The only near-hit is line 89, lowercase and incidental ('The logo is group-aware in the same way as the purchase order configuration'). ALL twelve sections bind to this page by GUIDE-SECTION ADJACENCY ALONE. INDEPENDENT ATTESTATION BY NAME EXISTS FOR ONLY FOUR: (1) Company Name Without Address - purchase-request-and-purchase-order-8b36ae07.md line 209 names the field in the Purchase Order Configuration window; (2) Company Branding Logo - line 89 of the roster file ties the logo to 'the purchase order configuration' and its group-awareness; (3) Company Address - preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md ties Body text/address/Instructions to the Purchase Order Configuration tool; (4) Supporting Documents - tools manage-images-03021850.md, 'The PO configuration associated with a Group may also include supporting documents.' and 'Administrators who configure purchase orders in PO Configuration'. THE OTHER EIGHT ARE ADJACENCY-ONLY: PO Number Generation, Message to Include on Transmitted Purchase Orders, Default Email Subject When Transmitting Purchase Orders, Default Email Message When Transmitting Purchase Orders, Default Sender Email, Fields to Appear on Purchase Orders, Ship To Without Requestor Name, Use Email as Bill-To. Every field node on this page MUST say in its notes which of the two it is. Adjacency is not attestation, and the deterministic validator cannot see this class of defect - it checks quotes against files, never controls against pages. UNENUMERATED FIELD LIST: 'Fields to Appear on Purchase Orders' - 'The header and line time fields you select will appear on the purchase order.' The selectable header and line-item roster is never enumerated anywhere in the corpus. Mark it unenumerated; do not guess. SAP TYPO TRAP: 'line time fields' is written for 'line item fields' in configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md - an extractor keyed on 'line item' misses it. NO LONG CATALOG ON THIS PAGE - measured: grep -c '^| ' = 0, grep -c '^-   ' = 0, grep -c '<table' = 0. The twelve are PROSE SECTION HEADINGS, not an enumeration. What makes the page tractable is that each carries a stated limit or constraint (9-char PO number, 3200-char message, 500-char email subject, .png/.jpg/.gif logo at 55px high / <=200px long / <=100KB, and a PurchaseOrder_DoNotReply@ConcurSolutions.com suffix that cannot be changed). GROUP SCOPE IS A PRECONDITION, NOT A FIELD: purchase-order-configuration-is-group-aware-b603f04b.md - 'Each PO configuration you create is based on the Group you select before creating the configuration.' and 'Groups with no PO configuration assigned use the Global Group configuration by default.' Corroborated cross-directory by manage-images-03021850.md, which is also the ONLY statement anywhere of how admin-uploaded and user-uploaded PO attachments interact. UI VARIANT: the corpus holds exactly five *-new-experience-* files (end-user-experience-85c2652b, policies-the-purchase-order-policy-5a1ba7ef, purchase-order-matching-rules-6c8fb80f, using-the-invoice-manager-page-f83ba5fa, using-the-unassigned-invoice-page-072e2f18) and NONE is PO Configuration. No variant labelling exists in either direction, hence 'undifferentiated' - do NOT claim 'new' or 'both'. TWO EXCLUDED SEEDS CONFIRMED EXCLUDED: purchase-order-processor-experience-8b507c54.md is an end-user processor topic that only points elsewhere for the tool, and purchase-order-setup-process-9f253ce7.md never names this tool at all (it is a setup-flow stop list, evidence about ordering, not a field source). Neither may be re-added. BOUNDARIES: 'Use Email as Bill-To' has prerequisites on Forms and Fields (the field must be added to the Purchase Order Header form) and Company Locations (a bill-to email address must be entered) - both already built, do not re-home. documentedBasis 'moderate' because real field-level documentation exists (twelve named settings, each with a stated limit or constraint, plus group scope and a cross-directory role gate) but the gaps are obvious and structural: eight of twelve are adjacency-only, the largest control is an unenumerated list, and there is no catalog, table, or value enumeration anywhere on the surface. coverageGuess 'partial' is driven by the unenumerated field list and the adjacency-only binding, not by missing files.

GATE: a rule set with In Use = Yes cannot be modified in any way; the admin must Copy it first, or unlock it by breaking the rule set's association to every invoice. THE UNLOCK CONTROL IS OFF THIS PAGE and is therefore NOT emitted as a field of this page (see dropped/change_to_non_po_action): it is the Actions-menu item on the My Invoices end-user page - 'In the Actions menu, click Change to Non-PO.' pages.verifyNotes: ASSEMBLED PROGRAMMATICALLY FROM THE THREE EXTRACTION FILES (python3, no retyping); only the nine repaired records were hand-authored, and every sourceQuote in the roster - carried or hand-authored - was re-verified mechanically against ROOT/<sourceFile> with a str.count containment check equivalent to grep -F -c. RESULT: 35/35 quotes verbatim, 0 failures; 35/35 sourceFile paths carry the correct '<guide-dir>/<filename>.md' shape (none repeats the CONCUR_INVOICE/ prefix defect); fromRawHtmlTable is false on all 35 and correct (grep -c '<table' = 0 on every cited file). No duplicate name and no duplicate LABEL survives on this page. COUNTS: 42 inputs (26 keep + 16 repair) -> 35 records out. 26 keeps carried through; 9 repairs emitted; 7 repair-bucket inputs moved to dropped (4 of them because the two refuters split on which of a pair of identical records survives, so the pair was merged into one; 3 because both refuters agreed the item is not a field of this page). NOTHING WAS SPLIT: 0 records were created during repair, per the hard constraint - four genuine split candidates are reported in splitsProposed instead. THE TWO REFUTERS DISAGREED FIVE TIMES AND EACH DISAGREEMENT WAS RESOLVED BY MERGE, NOT BY PICKING A WINNER'S RECORD WHOLE. name_field vs named_rules_group_name: named_rules_group_name survives (refuter 2's rename to matching_rule_name is not permissible - only input names may be emitted) but carries refuter 2's SUBSTANTIVE repair, so the 'named rules group' reading is now stated as INFERRED and the corpus ambiguity ('a descriptive name for the new rule' vs 'this named rules group') is recorded rather than settled. value_percentage_radio vs toleranceBasis: value_percentage_radio survives AND adopts toleranceBasis's fuller quote, the one that locates the control 'in the Tolerance section' and so distinguishes it from the Value/Percentage pair inside Overage Tolerance. level_field vs level: level_field survives (page-scoped identifier, avoids needless reuse against page.accounting-administration's 'Level'), carrying every word of level's four-enumeration analysis and the three dash spellings. group_conditions_dialog vs ruleGroupConditions: group_conditions_dialog survives because its name encodes the nested-window containment refuter 2 required to survive, with the twin's reach path, Insert/Save ownership and do-not-borrow-Audit-Rules warning merged in. change_to_non_po_action and match_status split the refuters on page ownership: change_to_non_po_action is DROPPED as a field (its only documenting topic opens 'In the My Invoices page...' - a field here would send a driver hunting for a button that is not there) with the full unlock sequence and the 2:1 label contradiction re-filed as an outbound prerequisite in the notes on in_use, exactly as refuter 1's corrected record specified; match_status is REPAIRED and KEPT because both refuters demanded its 6-value catalog stay attached to this page node and this roster shape has no page-level enumeration slot - it is emitted with fieldType corrected from 'table' to 'unknown', the better-scoped quote adopted, and its notes OPEN with the warning that it is not rendered or settable on this page. THAT IS THE ONE RECORD IN THIS ROSTER A HUMAN SHOULD LOOK AT: it is deliberately not a control. NO INVENTED VALUES ENTERED THE ROSTER. The single unsupported value the refuters found corpus-wide (ruleLevel's 'Line Item - Receipt', absent from its cited tools-guides file, which contains no occurrence of 'receipt' at all) was dropped with that record. No No/Yes pair was completed: in_use enumerates Yes and No inside its one cited clause, and allow_submit_approve keeps validValues EMPTY on purpose because only the selected state is documented. tolerance was REPAIRED from a four-value list to validValues [] because populating it picked one side of the contradiction the brief forbids reconciling; both readings are now recorded with their own verbatim quotes (step-3: 'Choose one tolerance:' -> None / Within (+/-) / Custom / Currency; configure-three-way L31: 'If applicable, in the Tolerance section, select None, Within, or Custom, and then select Value or Percentage.'). LONG CATALOGS - NOTHING SAMPLED OR TRUNCATED. Life to Date selection: 6 rows in source (the indented-table trap holds - grep -c '^| ' = 0, grep -cP '^\s*\|' = 22), 6 in the record with all six descriptions. Match Status: 6 values, all present. Confirmation types: 4 from the numbered prose catalog, with step-5's 3-row INVC/RIND/RCEN table correctly explained as excluding None rather than treated as a contradiction. Level: all four corpus enumerations preserved as a recorded contradiction. UI VARIANT 'both' IS EARNED, RE-VERIFIED IN THIS PASS, NOT INHERITED: I diffed the twins myself. Distinct loios (8b357dbb70891014bbdd65f9448c9095 vs 6c8fb80f969d446d88d994c0ed3444cb) on the same deliverable_loio, so this is a genuine variant pair and not a gerund/imperative republish; bodies are identical through line 36 except the '(New Experience)' title, and the New Experience file then appends material that already exists standalone (test-and-change-match-rule-sets, activate-exchange-rates). It contributes NO unique control, so no control is double-counted across the twins and every field record stays uiVariant 'undifferentiated'. Its only unique wording is the minority unlock label 'Change to Non PO Invoice option in the Actions menu', recorded as a 2:1 contradiction on in_use rather than reconciled. CONTRADICTIONS PRESERVED, NOT RECONCILED, in the records that carry them: tolerance 4-vs-3; tab depth (step-3 places the Rules tab one level up with no Edit Rules step, step-2 and configure-three-way place both tabs two levels down - majority tree is two levels down and a driver must probe both, recorded on edit_rules_button, rules_tab and life_to_date_tab); the three dash spellings of 'Line Item - Receipt'; the same-file label drift 'Matched against Received Quantity' (configure-three-way L27) vs 'Match against Received Quantity' (L60); the unlock label 2:1; Overage Tolerance's two options versus step-2's unlabelled three-option refinement on the same Life to Date tab. CORPUS DEFECT FLAGGED ON EVERYTHING TAKEN FROM IT: create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md is TRUNCATED (its body ends on a bare line containing only 'x', the only file corpus-wide that does), so matching_rule_type carries an explicit incompleteness warning and rule_groups_list flags the 'A Default rule set is provided' corroboration as coming from that file. COVERAGE GAPS REPORTED, NOT FABRICATED. (1) The Exception Message editor's EDIT control is attested in the same sentence as Change, New and Save but no lens emitted it, so a driver told to modify an EXISTING exception message has no record to drive - recorded on new_button and in splitsProposed. (2) The alternate open path 'Double-click the rule you want to use' is now recorded on edit_button; it is the only non-Edit-button way documented to open a rule set. (3) Rename commits with a KEYSTROKE ('pressing Enter when you are done'), not a button - now called out on rename_button. Neither refuter fabricated records for these and neither did I. OUTBOUND DEPENDENCIES LEFT OUTBOUND, NONE RE-HOMED: PO Matching Ruleset -> Policies (built); Delivery Slip Number and Purchase Order Number -> Forms and Fields (built); Is Purchase Order line Associated / Is Receipt Associated -> Audit Rules (built); 'Allow system to associate invoice lines to Purchase Order lines based on data attributes' -> Invoice Settings (built); receipt confirmation instructional text -> Localization (NOT built - this dependency legitimately stays unresolved); exchange rates -> Expense Admin module (outside Invoice entirely); Is Receipt Required -> set via PO Import, and it is the hard gate ('Unless the Receipt Required field is set to Yes, no receipt confirmation logic configured in Concur Invoice will be evaluated for that line.') carried in the notes on confirmation_type. VALUE SETS AND DEPENDENCIES ARE NOT IN THIS ROSTER'S SHAPE and must be taken from the three extraction files at merge time; the records here name the ones that must ride with them - notably the Line Item – Receipt pair set (contextField Level, EN DASH in the governing value) and the source-declared-partial amount-based set ('Line Item Total, Quantity, Tax, Shipping, etc.' - the 'etc.' is SAP's own) on payment_request_field, the two tolerance readings, the six Life to Date rows with descriptions, the six Match Status rows with cause descriptions, and step-5's INVC / RIND / RCEN codes with default message text on confirmation_type. NAVIGATION, unchanged from the map phase and not re-litigated: Administration > Invoice > Purchase Order Matching Rules, the only PO label in the corpus ever written with '(left menu)'; the middle nav node 'Invoice Processing Admin' is UNATTESTED for this page though documented for ~20 siblings on the same menu, so a driver must be prepared to try both. COVERAGE 'good' is my honest judgement, not inherited: 14 distinct corpus files carry a field-level sourceQuote and control-level documentation is dense and multi-topic (three enumerated list columns, a 6-row Life to Date table, a 4-value Level list, two tolerance lists, a 4-value confirmation-type catalog, Value/Percentage refinements, thirteen distinct buttons across five nested windows). The remaining must-read files are behavioural and conceptual rather than control-level and are consumed as corroboration, contradictions, dependencies and value sets - thin field yield from a rich prose topic is the right answer, not a miss. MUST-READ SKIPPED: none skipped for this lens; the page-level refuter findings confirm all 50 were consumed by at least one of the three lenses plus the two refutation passes, and I read the two New Experience/legacy twins directly in this pass to re-earn the uiVariant claim.

valueSets.context: The complete 6-row Selection | Description settings table on the Life to Date tab. UNCONDITIONAL - every row is offered whenever the Life to Date tab is open, and any combination may be activated ('Repeat by selecting a check box for each option you want to include.'). It is filed as a value set rather than left as the roster's flat array because each row carries a Description cell that tells a driver what the rule actually compares; the flat array carries names only.
valueSets.sourceQuote: Click the Life to Date tab, then select the check box next to the rule type to activate using the table below:
valueSets.notes: ALL SIX ROWS, NOTHING SAMPLED. Values are the Selection cells verbatim, in source order. The Description cell for each, verbatim: Gross Amount = 'Compares the purchase order gross amount to the cumulative gross sums of all invoices with this purchase order number.'; Net Amount = 'Compares the purchase order net amount to the cumulative net sum of all invoices with this purchase order number.'; Line Item Total = 'For each associated line item, compares the purchase order line item total to the cumulative line item totals of all invoices sharing this purchase order number.'; Line Item Quantity = 'For each associated line item, compares the purchase order quantity to the cumulative quantities of all invoices sharing this purchase order number.'; Match against Received Quantity = 'For each line item of the associated PO, this rule compares the total quantities invoiced (based on quantities matched) against the total quantities on associated receipts.'; Line Item Tax = 'For each associated line item, compares the purchase order tax to the cumulative taxes of all invoices sharing this purchase order number.' INDENTED-TABLE CASE: the whole table sits inside numbered step 4, so a '^|' census returns 0 for this file and 22 with leading whitespace allowed. LABEL DRIFT on the fifth value: configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md writes the past-tense 'Matched against Received Quantity' in its overview bullet ('the admin can select the Line Item ' + EN-DASH + ' Receipt rule in the Rules tab and the Matched against Received Quantity rule in the Life to Date tab') and the present-tense 'Match against Received Quantity' in its own numbered step 33 lines later; the canonical settings table quoted here uses the present tense. Do not assert either as the UI string. Published with the table: 'The system uses the Line Item Number to associate line items on the PO and invoice.' Corroborated in prose by the TRUNCATED create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md ('comparing Gross, Net, Line item total, Line item quantity, if matched against received quantities, and/or Line item tax') - that file's body ends on a bare 'x', so treat it as incomplete.

valueSets.context: READING A of the Life to Date tolerance refinement - the THREE options step-2 offers after a Life to Date check box is selected. Conditional on the check box, and the three are NOT flat alternatives: the source binds Value and Currency with '- AND -' and separates that pair from Percentage with '- OR -'.
valueSets.sourceQuote: As you select each check box, options appear that let you refine the tolerance.
valueSets.notes: CONTRADICTS READING B (the next set), which is the same control on the same tab labelled 'Overage Tolerance' with only two options and no Currency. NOT RECONCILED - both are emitted. Step-2 never gives this section a label at all; the label 'Overage Tolerance' exists only in configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md, which is why the roster field is named overage_tolerance and why attaching Reading A here is a wiring decision, not a corpus claim. Verbatim option text: Value = 'Specify a number at or above that at which the rule set will trigger an exception. For example, if the Value is 100 and the PO amount is 1000, invoice(s) at or above 1100 will trigger the exception.'; Currency = 'Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system.'; Percentage = 'Choose a percent above which the rule set will trigger a flag. For example, if the Percentage is 1 and the PO amount is 1000, invoice(s) above 1010 will trigger the exception.' The AND/OR structure is literal in the source: Value, then '- AND -', then Currency, then '- OR -', then Percentage - so a driver must not treat these as three mutually exclusive radio options. No currency roster is published anywhere in the corpus, so the Currency option's own list stays unenumerated (see field currency_field). Exchange-rate activation is NOT a control on this page: concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-matching-rules-new-experience-6c8fb80f.md states 'Exchange rates that allow currency conversion are on by default.' and 'As reference, this feature is accessed using the Expense Admin module.' - the Expense Admin module is out of scope for this graph.

valueSets.context: READING B of the same Life to Date tolerance refinement - TWO options under a section this topic names 'Overage Tolerance', reached after selecting the Match against Received Quantity option on the Life to Date tab. Currency is absent.
valueSets.sourceQuote: In the Overage Tolerance section, select Value or Percentage.
valueSets.notes: This is the ONLY attestation of the label 'Overage Tolerance' anywhere in the corpus. Do not merge with Reading A: this topic offers two options where step-2 offers three, and gives the section a name step-2 withholds. HYPOTHESIS ONLY, stated as such: Currency may be provisioning-dependent (visible only where multi-currency conversion is in play), or this topic may simply be scoped to the three-way-matching path. The corpus states neither. Worked semantics published here, verbatim: Value = 'Specify a number at or above that at which the rule set will trigger an exception. For example, if the Value is 100 and the Quantity Received on this PO line is 1000, invoice(s) at or above 1100 will trigger the exception.'; Percentage = 'Choose a percent above which the rule set will trigger a flag. For example, if the Percentage is 1 and the Quantity Received is 1000, invoice(s) above 1010 will trigger the exception.' Note the worked example differs from step-2's: here the baseline is the Quantity Received on the PO line, there it is the PO amount.

valueSets.context: READING A of the Rules-tab Tolerance control - the FOUR-option bullet run under the heading 'Choose one tolerance:'. Complete and in source order. The roster deliberately leaves this field's validValues empty because two irreconcilable lists exist; both are emitted here as separate sets.
valueSets.sourceQuote: Within (+/-): Choose this to specify a balanced amount of tolerance equal above and below that of the PO field being matched to the same request field
valueSets.notes: CONTRADICTS READING B (next set): four options here versus three there, 'Within (+/-)' here versus 'Within' there, and Currency present here and absent there. NOT RECONCILED. The quote deliberately carries the two discriminating features - the '(+/-)' suffix and the option's existence as an independent bullet in a four-item list. Full source text of the other three: 'None: Choose this to trigger the rule if any deviation is detected between the fields - no tolerance is permitted'; 'Custom: Choose this to create an asymmetrical amount of tolerance above and below that of the PO field being matched to the same request field'; 'Currency: Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system.' Currency is arguably a different axis from None/Within/Custom - the source nevertheless lists all four under one 'Choose one tolerance:' heading, and that is recorded as found, not corrected. The whole section is marked conditional at the step level: '(Optional depending on field choice) Determine what tolerance you will allow when the rule is triggered using options under Tolerance.' - so a driver must not assume Tolerance is present for every Payment Request / Purchase Order field pair. CONSEQUENCE FOR A DRIVER: probe the four-option list first; if only three appear, match on the prefix 'Within' rather than the exact string 'Within (+/-)', and do not fail the step because Currency is missing.

valueSets.context: READING B of the same Rules-tab Tolerance control - the THREE-option inline list in the three-way matching procedure, written without the '(+/-)' suffix and without Currency, and followed by a SECOND control (Value or Percentage) that Reading A never mentions at Rules-tab level.

valueSets.notes: Verbatim definitions: None = 'No receipt confirmation is required. This is appropriate for spend requiring only a two-way match between invoice and PO.'; Invoice = 'Presenting and confirming the invoice overall, within Concur Invoice, is sufficient to confirm receipt. valueSets.sourceQuote: The table below shows all possible Match Status types.

valueSets.context: Concur Receiving roles matrix - the complete 6-row x 4-column Role | What the User Can/Cannot Do | Where? | Conditions table published in this page's own tools-guides Required Roles topic.
values: Purchase Order Processor || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images. || In the transmitted purchase order. || None.
Invoice Processor || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images. || In Purchase Order tab of the opened invoice. || None.

Purchase Request User || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images || In the transmitted purchase order. || The admin must have selected (enabled) the Allow Purchase Request Owners to Edit their own Purchase Orders option in Invoice Settings. Alternatively, the user can have the Receipt User role.
Invoice User || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images. || In the Purchase Order tab of the opened invoice. || None.

Central Receiver || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images for all purchase orders in their group. Cannot transmit and process purchase orders or invoices. || In the transmitted purchase order. || The Concur Receiving feature must be activated.

Receipt User || Can add, edit, and delete receipts and receipt images. Can only add, edit, and delete receipt data for their own purchase orders. || In the transmitted purchase order. || The Concur Receiving feature must be activated.
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: None of these six roles is a control on either Group 3 page - role assignment happens in user administration, which is not a page in this graph. Attaching the matrix to rule_set_name (as one extraction lens did, defensively) would be a wrong owner: rule_set_name is a list-page column, not a role picker. ALL SIX ROWS AND ALL FOUR COLUMNS are reproduced above so the catalog is not silently lost; the ' || ' separator is MINE, added to keep one row per array entry, and every string between separators is verbatim except that the Purchase Request User's second cell genuinely lacks a trailing period in the source. Two multi-sentence cells (Central Receiver, Receipt User) are joined from two source paragraphs within one cell. Anchoring quote in the file: 'This table shows roles in Concur Invoice working with Concur Receiving and what they can and cannot do.' Also published in the same topic and worth carrying forward: 'Only the Invoice Configuration administrator can access and configure the Purchase Order Matching Rules feature.' and a Note that a user with the Purchase Order Processor or Purchase Order Processor (Audit) role can reach imported POs on entities without Purchase Request enabled. TOOLS-GUIDES ONLY - an admin-guides-skewed search loses this table entirely. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A Concur Receiving / Purchase Order page node (or a roles/permissions node) with a field that owns the role roster. The Purchase Request User row also carries a real cross-page dependency to the already-built Invoice Settings page, via the 'Allow Purchase Request Owners to Edit their own Purchase Orders' option - if a field of that name exists on Invoice Settings, this row can be wired as a dependency without inventing an owner here.

valueSets.context: The three matching METHODS the page's rule sets implement - a closed three-item catalog with definitions.
values: Two-Way Matching: Matching between invoices and purchase orders (no receipt)
Three-Way Matching: Matching between invoices and purchase orders and received quantities
Receipt Confirmation: Matching between invoices and purchase orders (including receipt confirmation that the order has been fully received)

Kept because it is a complete enumerated catalog and because it disambiguates the page's vocabulary for a driver. Anchoring quote: 'Concur Invoice offers three types of matching methods:'. Each of the three values above is verbatim, in source order. The tools-guides twin overview-8b4fd062.md republishes the same list nearly verbatim (differing only by 'Invoice does not check quantity' for 'Concur Invoice does not check quantity', a capitalised 'Suppliers', a missing abstract line and italics) - a cross-deliverable republish, NOT a UI variant, so it is not double-counted. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Nothing - and that is the finding. It should stay unwired unless SAP later documents a control that selects a matching method by name.

valueSets.context: The 6-term terminology glossary for this page's objects, published as a bullet run.
values: Concur Receiving: The ability for users to add quantity receipt data manually in Concur Invoice.
Purchase Order Payment Request: An invoice associated with a PO by the unique number associated with the PO.
Life to Date: The complete span of all invoices associated with their purchase order.
Associate: The relationship created when an invoice is linked to a PO by entering the unique PO number in the request header form.
Matching Rule Set: The combination of rules that is executed for every PO request matched under a given policy.
Named Rules Group: Any rule existing within ("under") the Matching Rule Set, for example, a condition-based rule group.
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: A glossary is not a field's option list. These are the authoritative object names for the page's node graph, not values an admin selects. Anchoring quote: 'The following terms are used throughout this document and within Invoice.' All six terms, verbatim and complete, in source order; the Matching Rule Set entry is cut at its first sentence, the source continuing 'Can be a simple, single rule, or more complex multiple match rule that includes "nested" condition-based rules run against custom fields that differentiate by spend type, project, or division as examples.' TERMINOLOGY TENSION worth flagging for a driver: 'Life to Date' is simultaneously a glossary concept, a tab name (life_to_date_tab) and a rule-type value (matching_rule_type), so a text match on those three words is ambiguous. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A glossary or vocabulary node type in the schema. It should never be wired to a field.

valueSets.context: The four events that RE-RUN an already-configured match rule set, and - separately - the three invoice states in which match rules CANNOT run at all.
values: On Header save and Line Item delete, save, and line sequence change
Changing Invoice Owner, Vendor, or reassigning an invoice
Upon PO import, if the import identifies a matching invoice in Concur Invoice that had not been previously associated to a PO
Upon receipt import for invoices associated to the PO
Is part of a payment demand
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: Runtime timing and eligibility, not a field's option list - no control on either Group 3 page selects when rules run. Kept in full because a driver needs it to predict when its configuration takes effect and why a correctly configured rule set can appear to do nothing. The two lists are concatenated in one record and are distinguishable by position: entries 1-4 are the re-run triggers, entries 5-7 the blocking states. Anchoring quotes: 'When these two things are true, rules are re-run whenever relevant changes are made to the invoice or to the PO. This includes:' and 'Has been extracted'. The seventh value keeps the source's markdown emphasis characters ('_Unassigned_') so it stays a verbatim substring. FIRST-RUN preconditions are separate and BOTH required: successful association to a PO - AND - the invoice in an assigned state; three-way matching adds association to received quantities. Published caveat: 'Rules are rerun for the changes listed above regardless of workflow status.' TOOLS-GUIDES ONLY. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A behaviour/trigger node type. As field values it has no owner and must not be given one.
