dependencies.condition: HARD LOCK. Edit is only usable while the selected rule set's In Use column reads No. When In Use is Yes the rule set cannot be edited or deleted at all; the documented ways forward are (a) Copy it, edit the copy, then change the PO Matching Ruleset value in Policies, or (b) unlock it by breaking every invoice association. A driver must read In Use before attempting Edit.
dependencies.sourceQuote: A rule set with an In Use status of Yes cannot be modified in any way.

dependencies.condition: The In Use value is not settable on this page - it is derived from whether the rule set is associated to any active invoice. The only documented way to drive it from Yes back to No is to break every invoice association, which the corpus describes as using the Change to Non-PO option in the Actions menu (an end-user/processor surface, not an admin configuration page - this endpoint will not resolve). NOTE the corpus also frames this as 'remove all associations to the policy' in access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md, a differently-worded description of the same unlock.
dependencies.sourceQuote: A matching rule set with a status of In Use can be unlocked by breaking its association with all invoices it is associated with.

dependencies.condition: Completing the Change to Non-PO reassignment for every associated invoice flips In Use to No and re-enables the Edit button on this page. Source endpoint is an end-user/processor page that is not part of this graph and will not resolve.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Now, the rule set has a status of No and can be edited using the Edit button:

dependencies.condition: THE LOAD-BEARING CROSS-GROUP EDGE. A rule set built here does nothing until a PO policy selects it in the PO Matching Ruleset field on the Policies page; that same field is the documented swap point when a locked (In Use = Yes) rule set has to be replaced by an edited copy. PO Matching Ruleset is a Policies field and must never be re-homed here.
dependencies.sourceQuote: You select a rule set using the PO Matching Ruleset option in Policies.

dependencies.condition: The Associated Policies column is a read-back of the Policies-side selection, not an editable control on this page. Its content changes only when a policy's PO Matching Ruleset value changes. A driver can use it to verify that a Policies edit took effect.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Associated Policies: Shows what Invoice PO policy has been configured to include this PO matching rule set.

dependencies.condition: SCOPING LIMIT, distinct from the edge above. Because the only binding a rule set has is its selection into a policy, the rule set inherits that policy's own attributes (the corpus names Region and Country) and nothing finer. Consequence stated verbatim in the same sentence's follow-on: 'Therefore, it is not possible to have different rules per expense type/account code.' So a driver must NOT look for an expense-type or account-code scope control on this page, and must not expect Expense Types to gate matching rules. The same limitation is republished as prose in general-notes-ced8d7d0.md (distinct loio); recorded once.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Rule sets are tied to their policy by selection as well as any attributes (such as Region or Country) that are specific to policy.

dependencies.condition: Row selection under Rule Set Name is the prerequisite for every action button on the list page: the rule set must be selected before Edit (and, per step-1, before Copy) will act on anything.
dependencies.sourceQuote: On the Purchase Order Matching Rules page, select the rule set, and then click Edit.

dependencies.condition: Creation is Copy-then-Rename-then-Done; there is no New button attested for this page anywhere in the corpus. Rename acts on the auto-generated 'Copy of...' entry that Copy produces, and the name is committed with the Enter keystroke, not a button.
dependencies.sourceQuote: then click Rename and type a descriptive name for the matching rule set

dependencies.condition: Inside an opened rule set, a named rules group must be selected in the Rule Groups list before Edit Rules will open the rules window for it. The corpus's worked example selects the seeded 'Default' group as the basis for a new group.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group).

dependencies.condition: OPTION-LIST DEPENDENCY. The Payment Request list is repopulated by the Level selection - which is exactly why the roster carries no enumerated value list for it. Level must be set first. The corpus never publishes the per-level field catalog; the only enumerated case is the Line Item - Receipt pair (Line Quantity and Received Quantity / Receipt Associated and Receipt Associated).
dependencies.sourceQuote: As different levels are chosen in Level, different field sets will populate the selections available in Payment Request and Purchase Order.

dependencies.condition: OPTION-LIST DEPENDENCY, second hop. Beyond the Level gating above, the Purchase Order list is further narrowed by the Payment Request field chosen in the immediately preceding step ('the step above'). Order for a driver: Level, then Payment Request, then Purchase Order.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Under Purchase Order, select the PO field to match to the invoice (they will change depending on the field selected in the step above).

dependencies.condition: AVAILABILITY DEPENDENCY, with a documented ambiguity. Tolerance is qualified '(Optional depending on field choice)', so the Tolerance section is not offered for every field pairing - but the corpus never says WHICH field choice governs, nor which pairings expose it. This edge points at purchase_order_field only because that is the step immediately preceding Tolerance in the same procedure; the governing selection could equally be payment_request_field. UNDETERMINED - do not treat the endpoint as settled.
dependencies.sourceQuote: (Optional depending on field choice) Determine what tolerance you will allow when the rule is triggered using options under Tolerance.

dependencies.condition: Add is the commit control on the Rules tab: a rule is not part of the set until Add writes it as a row into the grid at the bottom of the rules window. Nothing on the Rules tab persists on field selection alone.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Click Add to insert this rule into the rows under Rules.

dependencies.condition: Selecting a Life to Date rule check box reveals the tolerance refinement controls for that rule; they are not present beforehand. CONTRADICTION RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED: step-2 describes these revealed controls as UNLABELLED and offers Value AND Currency - OR - Percentage, whereas configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md calls the same area 'Overage Tolerance' and offers only Value or Percentage. The endpoint is written as overage_tolerance because that is the only attested label, but a driver may find no such label.
dependencies.sourceQuote: As you select each check box, options appear that let you refine the tolerance.

dependencies.condition: A configured exception message is not standing UI text - it surfaces to the end user only when the rule it was attached to actually triggers. So the message is scoped to one rule, and a driver verifying configuration cannot expect to see it except on a triggering invoice.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The Exception Message option is available on the Rules tab and will only display when the user triggers the configured rule.

dependencies.condition: Allow Submit/Approve is an override whose only effect is on invoices that have already breached the rule's tolerance and raised an exception; with no tolerance breach it changes nothing. Note the corpus documents only the SELECTED state of this check box - no cleared/No value is enumerated anywhere, and none is invented.
dependencies.sourceQuote: An invoice can be submitted and proceed to processing even if an exception is generated due to the tolerance limit of the matching rule set.

dependencies.condition: Condition-based ('Multiple') rule sets are built UNDER an existing named rules group: the parent group must be selected in the Rule Groups list before Add creates the condition group beneath it. This is a different use of Add from the Rules-tab Add that commits a rule row.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select the named rule group within which the condition-based rule set will be included, then click Add.

dependencies.condition: The condition must exist and be selected before Edit Rules can define what the system does when that condition is detected. Ordering inside step-4: configure conditions in the Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions window, Insert/Save them, then select the new condition and click Edit Rules.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select the new condition, and then click Edit Rules to specify what should happen when the system detects the condition

dependencies.condition: Inside a condition-based rule group, Update - not Add - is the control that writes the rule into the row, and it must be clicked after EACH rule before Save. A driver that clicks Save without Update loses the rule.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Click Update to add the rule to the row.

dependencies.condition: Confirmation Type is not on the rule-group form itself: Edit Confirmation opens the Select Confirmation Type window in which the type is chosen. The choice is made per rule group.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Do this by clicking Edit Confirmation to open the Select Confirmation Type window, choosing a confirmation type based on the rule group.

dependencies.condition: The receipt-confirmation instructional text a rule shows is bound to the field type chosen when the rule group's conditions were created in the Condition Editor. So the condition group must be built before confirmation text is meaningful, and changing the condition field type changes what the confirmation is associated with.
dependencies.sourceQuote: These are associated with the field type you select when creating the rule group conditions using the Condition Editor.

dependencies.condition: SPLIT OF CONCERNS ACROSS PAGES. The confirmation type chosen here decides WHICH message fires; the message TEXT is authored and translated only in the Localization tool (Administration > Invoice > Localization > select a language > Category column > Invoice Receipt Confirmations > Modify > Message column > Save). Default text for the three non-None types is published in step-5's table. FORWARD REFERENCE: Localization is not yet built in this graph, so this endpoint will not resolve until it is. Corroborated by confirmation-message-configuration-65b79d9c.md ('Admins configure messages in the Localization tool.'). TEXT TRAP: the source reads 'clickingAdministration' with no space.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This text can be customized from the default text and localized into other languages by clickingAdministration > Invoice > Localization to access this tool.

dependencies.condition: THE GATE ON THE WHOLE RECEIPT-CONFIRMATION FEATURE. Nothing configured on this page for receipt confirmation is evaluated for a PO line whose Is Receipt Required value is not Yes. That value is data on the PO line item set by PO Import - it is NOT a control on any admin page, so this endpoint will never resolve to a config page. SAP's own recommendation is to set it to Yes for all lines and let the matching rules decide the outcome, including None.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Unless the Receipt Required field is set to Yes, no receipt confirmation logic configured in Concur Invoice will be evaluated for that line.

dependencies.condition: A Line Item - Receipt (three-way) rule matches a SPECIFIC goods receipt note only if the Delivery Slip Number field has been added to the Payment Request Header form in Forms and Fields; absent that field, matching falls back to sequential receipt order. The field is added on Forms and Fields (Administration > Invoice > Forms and Fields > Form Type = Payment Request Header > Add Fields), never here. FORWARD REFERENCE AT FIELD LEVEL: Forms and Fields is built, but it is modelled generically (formType / addFieldsToFormsFieldSelector) and carries no per-invoice-field nodes, so 'Delivery Slip Number' is a named forward reference rather than an existing node.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If the admin does not add the Delivery Slip Number field to the form, Concur Invoice will perform the matching sequentially by receipt.

dependencies.condition: CONTRADICTION WITH THE EDGE ABOVE - BOTH RECORDED, NEITHER RECONCILED. admin-guides (delivery-slip-number-field-for-three-way-matching-b0d3f1ca.md) says matching falls back to sequential receipt order when the DSN field is absent; tools-guides (this quote) says that once a DSN IS specified and no GRN carries a matching DSN, Concur Invoice does NOT revert to sequential logic and leaves the invoice unassociated. The two describe different trigger conditions (field absent vs field present but unmatched) and may both hold, but the corpus never reconciles them. Consequence for a driver: an unassociated invoice line cannot satisfy a received-quantity rule. Same file: the detail-level DSN is read-only and copies down from the header, so every line of an invoice carries one DSN (SAP typo in source: 'header DNS field').
dependencies.sourceQuote: If Concur Invoice does not find a GRN with the same DSN, it will not revert to the sequential association logic but will instead leave the invoice unassociated to the GRNs.

dependencies.targetField: Allow system to associate invoice lines to Purchase Order lines based on data attributes
dependencies.condition: Line Item and Line Item - Receipt rules can only compare correctly identified lines, and the switch that decides HOW lines are identified - by data attributes (unit price, quantity, description, PO number) or, when cleared, sequentially line 1 to line 1 - lives on Invoice Settings, not here. FIELD-LEVEL FORWARD REFERENCE: Invoice Settings is a built page but does not currently carry this option as a field node, so the endpoint names it as documented; this is also a coverage gap worth reporting on Invoice Settings.
dependencies.sourceQuote: On the Invoice Settings page, toggle (enable) the Allow system to associate invoice lines to Purchase Order lines based on data attributes option.

dependencies.condition: COMPANION CONFIGURATION. The Is Purchase Order line Associated and Is Receipt Associated values that these audit-rule conditions test are produced by the PO matching rules configured on this page; the corpus lists building them as an optional step of Configure Three-Way Matching. Same source states the event gating: the two fields 'will be available when the admin selects the Payment Request Detail Save or the Payment Request Detail Submit events'. INFERRED: the corpus states the pairing and the ordering context but never says outright that the audit-rule fields are inert without matching rules configured.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The admin can create rules by using the Is Purchase Order line Associated or Is Receipt Associated fields in the Audit Rules tool.

dependencies.condition: The base-currency tolerance option converts alternate invoice currencies automatically, and that conversion is supplied by exchange rates that are ON BY DEFAULT and administered entirely outside Concur Invoice, in the Expense Admin module. There is NO exchange-rate control on this page and none should be invented; the endpoint is out of Invoice scope and will not resolve.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Activation of exchange rates enables default currency conversion for matching rule sets in the Expense Admin module.

dependencies.condition: DATA PRECONDITION for the Match against Received Quantity rule and for every Line Item - Receipt rule: receipt quantities must be getting into Concur Invoice first, by FTP import, by API, or by manual entry through Concur Receiving. Corroborated in configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md with the same three routes. The endpoint is a file/API interface, not an admin configuration page, so it will not resolve. Same file: clients needing three-way matching AND receipt confirmation must use both the Receipt Confirmation Import and the Quantity Receipt Import.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Before clients can start to use the Three-Way Matching feature, they need to import the Quantity Receipt file, which they can do through an FTP import, through the API, or by entering receipt data using Concur Receiving.

dependencies.condition: CROSS-GROUP ORDERING. Where receipts are entered manually rather than imported, the Receiving feature must first be turned on via Policies (Administration > Invoice > Policies > purchase request policy > PO Configuration section > Enable Concur Receiving > Save) before any receipt data exists for Match against Received Quantity or a Line Item - Receipt rule to evaluate. TEXT TRAP: the cited file's step 1 misspells the menu item as 'Polices'. Same file also notes a knock-on to Forms and Fields: 'Once this feature has been activated, the Purchase Order Receipt form in the Forms and Fields tool will automatically be used.'
dependencies.sourceQuote: Before users can start to work with and manage their receipts in Concur Invoice, the administrator needs to go to Administration > Invoice > Policies to activate the Receiving feature.

dependencies.condition: WHEN CONFIGURATION TAKES EFFECT - matters for verifying a change, not for making it. Rules first run only when the invoice is BOTH associated to a PO AND in an assigned state; for three-way matching the invoice must in addition be associated to received quantities. They re-run on header save, line item delete/save/sequence change, owner or vendor change or reassignment, a PO import that newly matches, and a receipt import - regardless of workflow status. They cannot run at all if the invoice has been extracted, is part of a payment demand, or has a status of Unassigned. This endpoint is a runtime condition, not an admin page, and will not resolve.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The invoice is in an assigned state (by any method, such as the Payment Request Import, Vendor to Employee rules assignment, AP User assigning to Invoice Owner, one Invoice Owner to another, etc.).

dependencies.condition: PAGE-WIDE SCOPE. Every setting on this page belongs to one Group, and the Group is chosen BEFORE the configuration is created - a driver that edits without establishing Group first will edit the wrong configuration. Same file states the fallback: 'Groups with no PO configuration assigned use the Global Group configuration by default.'
dependencies.sourceQuote: Each PO configuration you create is based on the Group you select before creating the configuration.

dependencies.condition: The logo carries the same Group-awareness as the rest of the configuration AND a hard cardinality limit of one logo per invoice group, so the intended Group must be selected before Upload. A second logo cannot be held within a Group - replacing means Remove then Upload. File-type and size constraints from the same section: .png, .jpg or .gif, 55 pixels high, no more than 200 pixels long and 100 KB.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The logo is group-aware in the same way as the purchase order configuration and clients can only update one company logo per invoice group.

dependencies.condition: Supporting documents belong to the PO configuration OF A GROUP and ride along with every PO the PO Processor transmits for that Group, so the Group must be established before upload. Cross-directory corroboration of the Group binding (this quote is from tools-guides).
dependencies.sourceQuote: The PO configuration associated with a Group may also include supporting documents.

dependencies.condition: The header and line-item field roster offered in this section is scoped by the Policy list selection, so Policy must be set before selecting fields. The corpus states the ordering only as a caution ('Ensure that you have selected...') and never describes the filtering mechanism, nor enumerates the selectable field roster anywhere - both UNDETERMINED. SAP TYPO in the same sentence: 'line time fields' is written for 'line item fields'.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Ensure that you have selected the correct policy in the Policy list.

dependencies.condition: HARD PREREQUISITE 1 OF 2. The Use Email as Bill-To field must first be added to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool; the wording is a precondition ('Provided the admin has added...'), so the control may be absent or inert on this page until that is done. FIELD-LEVEL FORWARD REFERENCE: Forms and Fields is built but modelled generically, with no per-invoice-field nodes.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Provided the admin has added the Use Email as Bill-To field to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool

dependencies.condition: HARD PREREQUISITE 2 OF 2, and this endpoint resolves: emailAddress is the existing Company Locations field node, attested cross-directory as present on the add and modify ship-to and bill-to windows (tools-guides/company-locations-8b49554d.md). Without an address there, the feature has nothing to send to and the PO falls back to the physical address: 'If clients have not configured this feature, the purchase order will use the physical address as it does today.' Capture-service clients may use their capture email address as the bill-to.
dependencies.sourceQuote: entered an email address in the bill-to email address field in the Company Locations tool

dependencies.condition: ACCUMULATION, NOT REPLACEMENT - the only statement anywhere in this corpus of how admin-uploaded and user-uploaded PO attachments interact. Documents uploaded here ride on every PO the Processor transmits for the Group, ALONGSIDE anything a user, approver or processor attached via the end-user Include in PO Transmission check box. The endpoint is an end-user/processor surface (Upload Image / Purchase Request Images / Preview Purchase Order), not an admin config page, and will not resolve. NOTE: the corpus documents NO link between PO supporting documents and the Image Handling admin page - no shared file-type or upload-permission constraint is stated - so no such edge is asserted here.
dependencies.sourceQuote: These documents apply to all PO transmissions performed by the PO Processor for that Group and are included alongside any documents added by the user.

dependencies.condition: The admin default set here is only the STARTING text: the PO processor sees it in the Preview Purchase Order window at transmittal review and may change it there per transmission. A driver verifying this setting must not expect the configured text to be what any given vendor received. Corroborated in tools-guides/preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md, which splits the responsibility explicitly - default text is changed in the Purchase Order Configuration tool, actual PO data is changed by the PO Processor on the PO itself. Endpoint is a processor window, not an admin page, and will not resolve.
dependencies.sourceQuote: note that this can be changed as you review the PO prior to transmittal

dependencies.condition: The prefix configured here is a default the PO processor can override per transmission; the suffix is immutable at BOTH levels (fixed as _DoNotReply@ConcurSolutions.com). Also from the admin-side section: if the prefix is left blank the system uses the requestor's email address as the From address, which SAP does not recommend because of spam risk. Endpoint is a processor window and will not resolve.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The processor can change the prefix for the From address but cannot change the suffix of the address

steps.name: Stand up a purchase order matching rule set end to end and put it into service on a policy
steps.goal: A named PO matching rule set exists, carries both kinds of sub-rule (Life to Date cumulative rules and Rules-type field-to-field rules) inside a named rules group, and is actually selected by a PO policy so invoices are evaluated against it. SILENT HALF-WORKS: (a) stop after Copy/Rename/Done and you own a correctly named clone of whatever rule set you copied - including its default rules - that nothing evaluates; (b) author the rules but never set PO Matching Ruleset on Policies and the set stays In Use = No forever and never fires; (c) leave the copied default rules in place and they keep firing alongside the rules you meant to add, because the corpus tells you to clear them explicitly; (d) once ANY invoice runs against it the set locks at In Use = Yes and can never be edited again - only copied - so this whole procedure must be finished before the policy is exposed to live invoices.

sequence.action: open the tool from the left menu and read the In Use column of the rule set you intend to copy from
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Read In Use BEFORE touching anything, because it decides whether the rest of this procedure is even legal on that row: a Yes locks the set permanently and forces the copy route (step grp3-replace-in-use-rule-set). A writer that skips this check will click Edit, get nothing, and misread a hard lock as a flaky control. SOURCE: "A rule set with an In Use status of Yes cannot be modified in any way." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md ROLE GATE, CORPUS-STATED: "Only the Invoice Configuration administrator can access and configure the Purchase Order Matching Rules feature." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/required-roles-ef2c2901.md

sequence.action: select an existing rule set row to serve as the base
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: There is no documented blank-create path on this page: creation IS copying, so a base row must be selected before Copy has anything to act on. Nothing else in the corpus attests a New button for a rule SET (New exists only inside the Exception Message editor). SOURCE: "In Purchase Order Matching Rules, select an existing rule set under Rule Set Name, and then click Copy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-create-the-purchase-order-matching-rule-set-4d3866f3.md

sequence.action: click to produce a "Copy of..." entry
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Copy is the container-creating act; every sub-rule authored in orders 6-19 lands inside the set this click produces, so nothing downstream has a home until it happens. SOURCE: "The PO matching rule set you create in this step will contain all sub-rule sets you configure in the steps below." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-create-the-purchase-order-matching-rule-set-4d3866f3.md

sequence.action: select the "Copy of..." row, click Rename, type the name, then press Enter
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Rename must happen while the copy is still the selected 'Copy of...' row - it is step 2 of a three-step wizard, not later housekeeping. The commit is a KEYSTROKE, not a button: a driver that types the name and clicks away loses it. The name is also the only handle the Policies page has on this set in order 20, so an unnamed copy cannot be bound. SOURCE: "Click the "Copy of..." to select it, then click Rename and type a descriptive name for the matching rule set, pressing Enter when you are done." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-create-the-purchase-order-matching-rule-set-4d3866f3.md NAMING CONVENTION, CORPUS-STATED for the first sets you build: "Copy the Default rule set, or your current rule set, and name it Test – Rule Set V1." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md

sequence.action: click to close the create wizard
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Done terminates the Copy > Rename > Done wizard and is distinct from the rule-set Save in order 19; the corpus then hands the sequence explicitly to the rule-authoring steps, which is why this step continues rather than ending here. SOURCE: "Continue to Step 2, Step 3, and Step 4 to add additional matching rules to the new PO matching rule." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-create-the-purchase-order-matching-rule-set-4d3866f3.md

sequence.action: reselect the newly named rule set and click Edit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The create wizard closes on Done and leaves you on the list page, so the set must be re-opened before any rule can be authored. Edit is also the control the In Use gate removes, which is why order 1 comes first. SOURCE: "On the Purchase Order Matching Rules page, select the rule set, and then click Edit." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md

sequence.action: select the Default named rules group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Default is a VALUE in this list, not a control, and the corpus states outright that it is the basis of the group you are about to author - pick the wrong group here and the rules in orders 9-18 attach to something the policy will never reach. SOURCE: "Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md

sequence.action: click to open the Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This is the window that actually contains the Life to Date and Rules tabs; without it the tabs are not reachable from the rule set. SOURCE: "Double-click the rule you want to use, and then, in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md CONTRADICTION - TAB DEPTH, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: step-3 skips Edit Rules entirely and places the tab one level up ("In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md). A driver must probe for the tabs at BOTH depths rather than fail on the first miss.

sequence.action: type a descriptive name for the new rule/rules group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Named before any rule type is selected, per the corpus order. The name is the identity the condition-based work in step grp3-condition-based-rule-group later selects against, so an unnamed group cannot be extended. SOURCE: "In Purchase Order Matching Rules, type a descriptive name for the new rule in Name." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md AMBIGUITY RECORDED: the sentence says 'a descriptive name for the new rule' while the surrounding topic is creating a named rules GROUP; the corpus does not settle which object is named. Do not assume.

sequence.action: click the Life to Date tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Life to Date is authored before the Rules tab because the corpus runs its own steps in that order and hands off explicitly at the end. SOURCE: "Proceed to Step 3 to add PO to Request fields matching rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.mdINFERRED:  beyond the hand-off: Life to Date rules compare against the CUMULATIVE sums of all invoices carrying the PO number, while Rules-type rules compare one invoice to one PO - so settling the cumulative envelope first gives the per-invoice rules a ceiling to sit inside. That reading is inferred from the two rule types' own descriptions, not stated as an ordering requirement.

sequence.action: select the check box next to each Life to Date rule type to activate
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The check box is what makes the tolerance controls exist at all - they are revealed per selection, so a driver that goes looking for a tolerance field before ticking a box will not find one. SOURCE: "As you select each check box, options appear that let you refine the tolerance." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md The six selectable rule types are enumerated in the canonical Life to Date table ("Click the Life to Date tab, then select the check box next to the rule type to activate using the table below:" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md).

sequence.action: set the tolerance basis for the selected Life to Date rule (Value, or Percentage)
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Set immediately after each check box, while its revealed options are on screen; deferring it leaves a rule armed with no stated tolerance. SOURCE: "In the Overage Tolerance section, select Value or Percentage." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: configure-three-way-matching names this section "Overage Tolerance" with exactly TWO options, while step-2 leaves the section unnamed and offers a THIRD - Value bound to Currency with "- AND -", or Percentage. Probe for both shapes; the corpus does not say which provisioning shows which.

sequence.action: if the Value branch is taken, choose the company base currency
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Only meaningful on the Value branch, and only in the step-2 reading of the tolerance section - which is why it sits after order 12 rather than beside it. Skip it on a Value tolerance and cross-currency invoices are compared against an unstated base. SOURCE: "Currency: Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system. This functions as for other rule sets, including audit rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md OFF-PAGE, DO NOT LOOK FOR A TOGGLE HERE: the exchange rates this relies on are on by default and administered outside Invoice — "Exchange rates that allow currency conversion are on by default. As reference, this feature is accessed using the Expense Admin module." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/activate-exchange-rates-for-matching-rule-sets-c51af31c.md

sequence.action: (optional) click Change to open the exception message editor
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Change is the only documented door into the message editor; New and Save in orders 15 and 19 are controls INSIDE it, not on the rule window, so clicking them first is a category error. SOURCE: "Exception Message: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md

sequence.action: (optional) click New inside the editor and author the exception text
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Authored while the editor is open and committed with the editor's own Save before returning to the rule window. Scope warning that a driver will otherwise get wrong: this New creates a MESSAGE, never a rule set - rule-set creation is Copy > Rename > Done at orders 3-5. SOURCE: "Exception Message: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md

sequence.action: (optional) select the check box to let the invoice move despite the exception
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Decided on the same pass as the message, because together they define what the triggered rule DOES; leave it clear and every trip of this rule becomes a hard stop rather than a flag, which is a policy decision, not a default to assume. steps.name: Configure three-way matching (invoice to PO to receipt) with receipt confirmation
steps.goal: Invoice lines are validated against both the purchase order and the goods receipts, with a Rules-tab Line Item - Receipt rule, a Life to Date Match against Received Quantity rule, a tolerance, an exception message, and a receipt confirmation type that tells the invoice owner what to do. SILENT HALF-WORKS: (a) build the rules before the Quantity Receipt file is imported and every line looks unreceived; (b) build only one of the two rules and the vendor recommendation of using all three is not met - the quantity envelope or the per-line check is missing with no error; (c) add the Delivery Slip Number field AFTER the rules are live and matching silently changes from sequential-by-receipt to DSN-targeted, with no fallback when no GRN carries the number; (d) configure any confirmation type without Is Receipt Required = Yes on the PO line and none of it is ever evaluated.

sequence.action: select the Payment Request Header form type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: FIRST, and this is the ordering fact that costs the most if missed: whether the Delivery Slip Number field exists on the header form decides what a Line Item - Receipt rule actually associates against. Add it later and the association logic changes underneath rules that are already live. SOURCE: "In the Form Type list, select the Payment Request Header form." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md CORPUS-STATED consequence of skipping it entirely: "If the admin does not add the Delivery Slip Number field to the form, Concur Invoice will perform the matching sequentially by receipt." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delivery-slip-number-field-for-three-way-matching-b0d3f1ca.md

sequence.rationale: INFERRED: The form list only populates after a form type is chosen, so this cannot precede order 1; inferred from the already-built Forms and Fields page record for formsTabList, whose own evidence states the list appears once a form type is selected. No new claim is made here.

sequence.action: select the Delivery Slip Number field in the Add Fields to Forms window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This is the optional leg the three-way matching topic names, and it is a decision with teeth rather than a cosmetic addition. SOURCE: "the admin should add the Delivery Slip Number field to the Payment Request Header form in the Forms and Fields tool." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md HARD NEGATIVE a driver cannot infer, CORPUS-STATED: once DSN is in play there is NO fallback — "If Concur Invoice does not find a GRN with the same DSN, it will not revert to the sequential association logic but will instead leave the invoice unassociated to the GRNs." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/receipt-association-and-three-way-matching-12b976a5.md

sequence.action: click Add Fields to commit the field onto the form
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Commits order 3; until this fires the field is selected but not on the form, and the matching behaviour is still the sequential one. The import itself is a file interface, not an admin page in this graph.

steps.name: Add a condition-based rule group to an existing named rules group (Multiple Matching Rule Sets)
steps.goal: One matching rule set carries several named rules groups, with a condition-based group nested under an existing group so that a different set of tolerances fires for a specific vendor, division, project or spend type. SILENT HALF-WORKS: (a) configure the conditions but never open Edit Rules on the new condition and you have a condition that detects something and then does nothing; (b) click Save in the conditions dialog but never Update after each rule and the rules do not land in the row; (c) attach the confirmation type to the wrong object - it can be set on the rule SET or on a rule CONDITION, and the two behave differently.

sequence.action: check the In Use status of the target rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Same gate as every other edit on this page, and it bites hardest here because condition-based groups are usually added to a set that has already been in service. In Use = Yes means this whole procedure is impossible on that row; you must copy it first. SOURCE: "A rule set with an In Use status of Yes cannot be modified in any way." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md

sequence.action: select the matching rule set and click Edit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The corpus opens this procedure exactly here; the condition-based group is added inside an existing set, never created standalone. SOURCE: "Select the matching rule set in Purchase Order Matching Rules and then click Edit." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: click Edit to open the rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Opens the set for editing; without it the rule groups list below is not reachable. SOURCE: "Select the matching rule set in Purchase Order Matching Rules and then click Edit." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: select the named rule group the condition-based group will sit under
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The parent group must be selected BEFORE Add, because the new group is created 'under' whatever is selected - Add with the wrong parent selected buries the conditions in the wrong branch of the set. SOURCE: "Select the named rule group within which the condition-based rule set will be included, then click Add." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.mdINFERRED:  Why this matters at all: the corpus describes the result as a set that can run across different PO types, with the conditions deciding which branch applies. Nesting under the wrong parent therefore mis-scopes the rules rather than erroring.

sequence.action: click Add to create the condition-based group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Same label as the Rules-tab Add in the end-to-end step but a different act entirely: here it creates a nested group, there it commits a rule row. A driver must resolve Add by context, not by label. SOURCE: "Select the named rule group within which the condition-based rule set will be included, then click Add." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: configure the detection conditions in the group conditions dialog
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Conditions are authored before any rule, because they are what the rules will hang off; a rule authored first has no condition to be triggered by. SOURCE: "In Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions, configure the conditions that the system will detect and then execute the matching rule set on" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md This is a NESTED WINDOW of this page with no independent click path - do not treat it as a page.

sequence.action: click Insert for each additional condition, then Save the dialog
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Insert is per-condition and Save closes the dialog: Save without Insert loses the pending condition. SAP typo preserved in the source ('any addition conditions'). SOURCE: "Click Insert to add any addition conditions, and then click Save when you are done." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: select the new condition and click Edit Rules
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: THE STEP THAT IS EASIEST TO SKIP AND THE MOST DAMAGING TO SKIP: without it the condition is detected and nothing happens. Edit Rules on the NEW CONDITION - not on the parent group - is what specifies the consequence. SOURCE: "Select the new condition, and then click Edit Rules to specify what should happen when the system detects the condition" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: click Update after each rule to add it to the row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Update, not Add, is the commit inside the condition-based branch, and it is per-rule: author several rules and click Update once and only the last survives. SOURCE: "Add any additional rules, clicking Update after each new rule to add it to the row, then click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: click Save to commit the condition-based group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Terminal commit, explicitly after the last Update in the same sentence. SOURCE: "Add any additional rules, clicking Update after each new rule to add it to the row, then click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: (optional) select the rule set or the rule condition and click Edit Confirmation
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Deliberately after the conditions exist: the corpus binds the confirmation text to the field type chosen when the rule group conditions were created, so doing this before order 6 has nothing to bind to. SOURCE: "These are associated with the field type you select when creating the rule group conditions using the Condition Editor." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-5-change-localize-receipt-confirmation-type-instructional-text-5328a8e1.md

sequence.action: (optional) choose the confirmation type for this rule group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Chosen per rule group, which is why it belongs at the end of the condition work rather than at the top of it. SOURCE: "Do this by clicking Edit Confirmation to open the Select Confirmation Type window, choosing a confirmation type based on the rule group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-5-change-localize-receipt-confirmation-type-instructional-text-5328a8e1.md OPEN LEG, NOT EMITTED AS A SEQUENCE ENTRY: changing or localizing the instructional text itself is done on the Localization tool, which is not yet a page in this graph — "This text can be customized from the default text and localized into other languages by clickingAdministration > Invoice > Localization to access this tool." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-5-change-localize-receipt-confirmation-type-instructional-text-5328a8e1.md

steps.name: Change the matching rules on a rule set that has locked at In Use = Yes
steps.goal: A live PO policy ends up running amended matching rules even though the rule set it was running is permanently locked. SILENT HALF-WORKS AND HARD FAILURES: (a) trying to edit the locked set directly - it cannot be edited OR deleted, ever; (b) editing the copy and stopping there, leaving the policy still bound to the old locked set, so nothing changes in production while the admin believes it has; (c) taking the unlock route on a large invoice population - the corpus only calls it feasible when the number of associated invoices is small.

sequence.action: read the In Use column for the rule set that needs changing
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The whole branch turns on this one value. Yes is not a warning, it is a permanent lock on that object. SOURCE: "once a match rule set is run against a PO associated invoice a status of In Use is assigned and the rule set is locked: it cannot be edited or deleted from the system." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md ALTERNATIVE ROUTE, DELIBERATELY NOT EMITTED AS A SEQUENCE ENTRY BECAUSE ITS CONTROL IS NOT ON AN ADMIN PAGE: "A matching rule set with a status of In Use can be unlocked by breaking its association with all invoices it is associated with." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md; the control lives in the Actions menu of the end-user invoice list ("In the Actions menu, click Change to Non-PO." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/change-a-po-based-invoice-policy-to-a-non-po-based-invoice-policy-12786d77.md), and its LABEL IS CONTRADICTED across three topics - "Change to Non-PO", "Change to Non PO Invoice", and the imperative form above. After it succeeds: "Now, the rule set has a status of No and can be edited using the Edit button:"

sequence.action: select the locked rule set row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The locked set is the base to copy from, so it is selected rather than opened - a driver that tries Edit here gets nothing and may misread the lock as a broken control. SOURCE: "The administrator is restricted to editing only those PO matching rules that do not have a status of In Use." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md

sequence.action: click Copy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Copy is the prescribed escape from the lock, and it is first because the whole remedy is a copy-edit-swap, in that order. SOURCE: "use the Copy button to create a copy, edit the rule set as needed, then change the PO Matching Ruleset value in Policies to implement the new rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md

sequence.action: rename the copy, incrementing the version, and press Enter
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Naming discipline is load-bearing here rather than cosmetic: because every tested set locks, a tenant accumulates versions, and the corpus prescribes an incrementing convention so the production set can be identified later. SOURCE: "Repeat steps 1–3 for any additional changes, incrementing the version name each time." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md

sequence.action: click Done to close the copy wizard
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Closes the Copy > Rename > Done wizard before the copy can be opened for editing; it is not the rule-set Save. SOURCE: "3.  Click Done." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-create-the-purchase-order-matching-rule-set-4d3866f3.md

sequence.action: select the copy and click Edit, then amend its Life to Date and Rules configuration
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Edit works on the copy precisely because the copy has never run against an invoice, so its In Use is still No. The amendment itself follows the same two sub-procedures as the end-to-end step. SOURCE: "Change the matching rules configuration by following the procedures under Step 2: Create the Life to Date Matching Rule Set and Step 3: Create the PO to Request Fields Matching Rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md

sequence.action: click Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Commits the amended copy before the policy is pointed at it - swap first and the policy briefly runs a half-edited set against live invoices, which would lock it in that state. SOURCE: "4.  Click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md

sequence.action: open the policy currently bound to the locked rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Which policy to open is read off the locked set's own Associated Policies column, so this order depends on order 1 having been read properly. SOURCE: "Associated Policies: Shows what Invoice PO policy has been configured to include this PO matching rule set." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md

sequence.action: change the selection to the amended copy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: THE STEP THAT ACTUALLY CHANGES PRODUCTION. Everything before it is preparation; skip it and the policy keeps running the locked original while the admin believes the fix shipped. SOURCE: "use the Copy button to create a copy, edit the rule set as needed, then change the PO Matching Ruleset value in Policies to implement the new rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md The corpus states the same remedy as an ordered test loop: "Make edits, and, when you are finished, apply the rule set to the relevant policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md

sequence.action: read Associated Policies back on both rows to confirm the swap
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The only documented read-back that the binding moved. It is a display of the Policies selection, never an editable field on this page. SOURCE: "You select a rule set using the PO Matching Ruleset option in Policies." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md

steps.name: Configure a group-aware purchase order: numbering, transmittal messaging, branding and printed fields
steps.goal: One invoice group's purchase orders are generated with the intended number sequence and transmitted to vendors with the right company identity, message, sender address, attachments and printed field set. SILENT HALF-WORKS: (a) configure without first selecting the Group and the settings land on the wrong configuration - and a group that never gets one silently falls back to the Global Group; (b) set the Next Sequence casually and you are stuck, because once the system is in use the number can only be moved further along, never back; (c) pick the printed fields without first setting the Policy list and you have chosen fields for the wrong policy.

sequence.action: select the invoice Group this configuration is for, before creating or editing anything
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: FIRST, and the corpus says so in the plainest possible terms. Every field below is scoped by this choice; set them with the wrong group selected and they land on another subsidiary's transmittals. SOURCE: "Each PO configuration you create is based on the Group you select before creating the configuration." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-configuration-is-group-aware-b603f04b.md AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT, CORPUS-STATED: "Groups with no PO configuration assigned use the Global Group configuration by default." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-configuration-is-group-aware-b603f04b.md: a group you forget simply inherits, with no error to notice. LOCATION UNATTESTED - REAL GAP, NOT AN OMISSION: the corpus never states WHERE the Group is selected; no Group control is documented on the tool itself. A driver must probe, not assume a picker on this page. ROLE GATE, CORPUS-STATED: "The Purchase Order Configuration tool is available to the Invoice Configuration administrator for setting default information for purchase orders. To view this tool, click Administration > Invoice > Purchase Order Configuration." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/use-the-purchase-order-configuration-tool-51009c8c.md

sequence.action: enter the starting PO number in the PO Number Generation section
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Do this before the system is in use, because afterwards it is one-way: the number can only be reset to one further along the sequence. There is also a 9-character limit on the PO number. SOURCE: "What you enter in the Next Sequence field will be the starting number, which can be altered once the system is in use only by using a number "further along" the numbering sequence in use" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md PLAN THE TEST NUMBERS DELIBERATELY, CORPUS-STATED: "TIP: For testing, plan your sequential number assignment so that, once testing is completed, the starting number sequence for production is what you want." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md.INFERRED:  UNDETERMINED, DO NOT ASSUME: whether the 9-character limit applies to the sequence alone or to prefix + sequence + postfix combined is never stated in this corpus.

sequence.action: set the PO number prefix
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Set alongside the sequence rather than later, because prefix, sequence and postfix compose one generated number and the 9-character ceiling is stated for the number as a whole. SOURCE: "The prefix and postfix of the PO number do not distinguish between uppercase and lowercase." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md LABEL WARNING: the corpus only ever writes this control in lowercase inside a Note ('prefix'), never as an on-screen label - a driver must probe for it rather than match a literal string.

sequence.action: set the PO number postfix
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Same composition reason as order 3, and case-insensitive for the same stated reason. The only content guidance is a convention, not a rule, and no maximum length is documented for the postfix itself. SOURCE: "Typically, the Postfix value is the initials of the purchasing agents." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: enter the instructions that ride on the transmitted PO itself
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This message is printed on the purchase order, not in the carrying email - conflating it with the two email fields below is the classic mistake, and produces vendor instructions that never reach the document. SOURCE: "Enter instructions you want the vendor to note and follow." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md HARD LIMIT, CORPUS-STATED: "This field is limited to 3200 characters." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md. Do not carry this limit to the email fields.

sequence.action: set the default subject line for PO transmission emails
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Governs the carrying email, not the document - the counterpart to order 5. SOURCE: "The text entered in the Default Email Subject When Transmitting Purchase Orders field will appear in the subject field of the email sent to the vendor (the admin can customize this field)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md HARD LIMIT, CORPUS-STATED: "This field is limited to 500 characters." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md. UNENUMERATED: the corpus says a tool tip offers tokens for this field but NEVER lists them; do not import a token catalogue from any other topic.

sequence.action: set the default body text for PO transmission emails
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This one is a DEFAULT, not a lock - the corpus states it can be changed at review time before transmittal, so a writer should not treat a per-PO deviation as a configuration failure. No character limit is documented for this field; do not carry over the 3200 or 500 figures. SOURCE: "The text entered in the Default Email Message When Transmitting Purchase Orders field will appear in the body of the email sent to the vendor (note that this can be changed as you review the PO prior to transmittal):" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: enter the company address that prints on the PO
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Part of the group-varying company identity, so it belongs after the Group is settled in order 1. SOURCE: "Enter your company address in the Company Address field." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md FENCE: this is a single free-text address printed on the PO PDF. It is NOT the structured Ship To / Bill To address-book records on the already-built Company Locations page. Do not merge or re-home.

sequence.action: click Upload in the Company Branding Logo section
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Group-scoped and singular, which is exactly why order 1 has to be right first - there is one logo per invoice group and uploading under the wrong group overwrites that group's brand. SOURCE: "The logo is group-aware in the same way as the purchase order configuration and clients can only update one company logo per invoice group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md CONSTRAINTS, CORPUS-STATED: "The image should be 55 pixels high and no more than 200 pixels in length and 100 KB in size." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md, which also enumerates the accepted formats and the View / Remove controls.

sequence.action: type the desired prefix for the sender address
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Only the prefix is editable; the suffix is fixed. Leaving it BLANK is not a neutral default - it changes the From address to the requestor's own, which SAP explicitly does not recommend because of spam filtering. SOURCE: "If the prefix is left blank, the system will use the requestor’s email address as the "From" address." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md SCOPE CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: the same prefix lever is also given to the PO Processor at transmit time — "The processor can change the prefix for the From address but cannot change the suffix of the address" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md. So the configured value can be overridden downstream by a different role.

sequence.action: upload the documents that should ride along with every PO transmittal for this group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Group-scoped like the logo, so again strictly after order 1. These are additive, not exclusive - they do not replace what the user attaches. SOURCE: "These documents apply to all PO transmissions performed by the PO Processor for that Group and are included alongside any documents added by the user." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/manage-images-03021850.md CORPUS-STATED effect: "These documents will be included when the supplier receives the PO." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: select the correct policy in the Policy list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: BEFORE the field selection below, and the corpus makes this an explicit instruction rather than an inference. Choose the printed fields with the wrong policy selected and you have configured a different policy's purchase orders. SOURCE: "The header and line time fields you select will appear on the purchase order. Ensure that you have selected the correct policy in the Policy list." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md SAP TYPO PRESERVED: the source writes 'line time fields' for 'line item fields'. UNENUMERATED: the corpus never lists which policies appear here. Policy definition itself lives on the already-built Policies page; this is only the selector that scopes the field roster.

sequence.action: select the header and line item fields to print on the purchase order
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Strictly after order 12, per the same sentence. UNENUMERATED, AND THE GAP IS THE FINDING: the selectable header and line-item field roster is never listed anywhere in this corpus, so a driver must read the live list rather than expect a known set. SOURCE: "The header and line time fields you select will appear on the purchase order. Ensure that you have selected the correct policy in the Policy list." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: (optional) select the header field that suppresses the requestor's name from the ship-to address
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: Grouped after order 13 because the corpus describes it as a header field, i.e. a member of the same (unenumerated) printed-field roster, given its own explanatory paragraph. The ordering is inferred from that membership, not stated. CORPUS-STATED effect: "Instead, they can use the Ship To without Requestor Name header field, whereby the requestor’s name is omitted." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md LABEL DRIFT, RECORDED: the section heading capitalises 'Without' and the body sentence lowercases it, in the same file. Probe both.

sequence.action: (optional) select the header field that removes the company address from the transmitted PO
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: Same membership and same reasoning as order 14 - a header field within the printed-field roster, so it follows order 13. CORPUS-STATED purpose, for cross-country PO creation: "Admins can select the Company Name without address header field for users who create purchase orders across countries and want to remove the purchase requester’s company address that is displayed on the transmitted purchase order." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md NOTE the interaction a writer should think about before setting it: order 8 fills a company address in precisely so it can print. This field suppresses it.

steps.name: Make purchase orders carry an email bill-to address instead of a physical one
steps.goal: Vendors receiving a transmitted PO see an email bill-to address that tells them where to send the invoice, instead of the physical address. THE FAILURE MODE IS ENTIRELY SILENT: if any of the three legs is missing the purchase order simply keeps printing the physical address exactly as before, with no error, no warning and nothing on the configuration page to indicate the feature is inert.

sequence.action: select the Purchase Order Header form type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The whole ordering of this step is corpus-stated in one sentence, which makes both form work and address work PRECONDITIONS of the configuration selection, not companions to it: the admin can select the header field only 'provided' both are already done. SOURCE: "Provided the admin has added the Use Email as Bill-To field to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool and entered an email address in the bill-to email address field in the Company Locations tool" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md Note the form is the PURCHASE ORDER Header form here, not the Payment Request Header form used by the Delivery Slip Number leg of three-way matching.

sequence.action: select the specific PO header form and open Add Fields
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: The form list only populates after a form type is chosen, so this cannot precede order 1; inferred from the already-built Forms and Fields page record, not from any new claim in this run.

sequence.action: select the Use Email as Bill-To field
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Leg one of the stated precondition. Without the field on the form there is nothing for the configuration selection in order 8 to expose. SOURCE: "Provided the admin has added the Use Email as Bill-To field to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool and entered an email address in the bill-to email address field in the Company Locations tool" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: click Add Fields to commit the field onto the form
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: Commit for order 3; the field is not on the form until the confirm control fires. Inferred from the already-built Forms and Fields add-fields procedure, whose confirm control is this field.

sequence.action: open the Bill To tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Leg two, and it must be the Bill To side specifically - a ship-to record carries no bill-to email for the PO to use. SOURCE: "Provided the admin has added the Use Email as Bill-To field to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool and entered an email address in the bill-to email address field in the Company Locations tool" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: create or open the bill-to location record
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: A location record must exist before an email address can be stored on it; inferred from the already-built Company Locations page structure, where the address record is the container for the email field in order 7.

sequence.action: enter the bill-to email address
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This is the value the vendor will actually be told to send the invoice to, so an empty one is exactly the silent-failure case in this step's goal. SOURCE: "The bill-to address on the PO PDF that the vendor receives is an email address which notifies the vendor to send the PO to the specified email address." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md CORPUS-STATED variant for capture clients: "Clients who use the capture service can use their capture email address as the bill-to address." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md.

sequence.action: click Save to store the address
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: Commit for orders 6-7 on the already-built Company Locations page; an unsaved address is not visible to the purchase order at transmit time.

sequence.action: select the correct policy in the Policy list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Same gate as in the group-aware configuration step: the header field roster is scoped by the selected policy, so selecting the bill-to header field before setting this configures the wrong policy's purchase orders. SOURCE: "The header and line time fields you select will appear on the purchase order. Ensure that you have selected the correct policy in the Policy list." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: select the bill-to header field within the printed field roster
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: The control being set in order 11 is described by the corpus as a 'header field', i.e. a member of this (unenumerated) roster, so it is reached through this control. That containment is inferred from the wording 'header field'; the corpus never enumerates the roster, so a driver must read the live list.

sequence.action: select Use Email as Bill-To
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: LAST, because the sentence that documents it makes it conditional on orders 1-8 having already happened. And the consequence of getting the order wrong is invisible rather than loud. SOURCE: "If clients have not configured this feature, the purchase order will use the physical address as it does today." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

contradictions.topic: The header-field control that suppresses the company address is written "Company Name Without Address" in title case as a section heading and "Company Name without address" in lowercase in the running prose and in the only cross-file topic that binds it to this window.

readings.summary: The settings roster topic titles the section in title case, with a capital W on Without and a capital A on Address.
readings.sourceQuote: Company Name Without Address

readings.summary: The body sentence immediately beneath that heading, in the same file, writes the control lowercase and calls it a header field.
readings.sourceQuote: Admins can select the Company Name without address header field

readings.summary: The purchase request and purchase order guide revision history — the only place in either guide directory that names this control and the Purchase Order Configuration window together — writes it lowercase.
readings.sourceQuote: Added information about the Company Name without address field in the Purchase Order Configuration window.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Match this control case-insensitively. Probe 'Company Name without address' first — two of the three attestations use that casing, including the only by-name page binding — and fall back to the title-cased 'Company Name Without Address' from the section heading. Never fail the step on a case mismatch alone, and never treat the two spellings as two different controls.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS, stated as a hypothesis: SAP title-cases settings-section headings mechanically while the body prose preserves the literal on-screen string, which would make the LOWERCASE form the more likely real UI label. The corpus never shows the rendered control, so nothing settles it. Merged from two raw records (crosscut lens, tables lens) that described the same disagreement; readings deduplicated on (sourceFile, sourceQuote).

contradictions.topic: The header-field control that omits the requestor's name from the ship-to address is written "Ship To Without Requestor Name" in the section heading and "Ship To without Requestor Name" in the body sentence of the same topic.

readings.summary: The section heading capitalises Without.
readings.sourceQuote: Ship To Without Requestor Name

readings.summary: The body sentence immediately beneath that heading lowercases without, in the only sentence anywhere in either guide directory that describes the control's behaviour.
readings.sourceQuote: they can use the Ship To without Requestor Name header field, whereby the requestor’s name is omitted.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Match case-insensitively and probe both forms; prefer the lowercase-'without' form, since that is the reading that survives in the one cross-file attestation available for the structurally identical Company Name control. Do not treat the two spellings as two different controls — they are one field.
contradictions.notes: WEAKER THAN contr.g3.001, AND SAID SO PLAINLY: both readings come from the SAME file, because no other topic in either guide directory mentions Ship To Without Requestor Name at all. This is intra-file heading-versus-prose drift, not a documented UI variant, and it is recorded only because a case-sensitive driver would fail on it — not because two sources disagree about the product.

contradictions.topic: Who owns the From-address prefix for PO transmission emails, and at what point in the lifecycle — the Invoice Configuration administrator on the Purchase Order Configuration tool, or the PO processor at transmit time in the Preview Purchase Order window.

readings.summary: The admin-guides settings roster places the prefix on the Default Sender Email field of the configuration tool and assigns the change to admins, with a documented default of PurchaseOrder.
readings.sourceQuote: type in a desired prefix in the Default Sender Email field

readings.summary: The tools-guides preview topic gives the same prefix lever to the PO processor inside the Preview Purchase Order window, at transmit time, well after the configuration is set.
readings.sourceQuote: The processor can change the prefix for the From address but cannot change the suffix

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Set the prefix in Purchase Order Configuration, but do NOT treat the configured value as authoritative on the wire: verify the actually-sent From address on a transmitted PO rather than asserting it from configuration alone, and do not build any check that assumes the configured prefix is what the vendor sees. Both topics agree the _DoNotReply@ConcurSolutions.com suffix is immutable, so only the prefix is in dispute.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS, stated as a hypothesis: these are probably COMPLEMENTARY surfaces rather than a genuine product conflict — the admin sets a default and the processor overrides it per transmission. The corpus never says so. It never states whether the processor's change is per-transmission or persists, never states whether it writes back to the configuration, and never states which wins if both are set. Recorded because the ambiguity is material to anyone configuring the sender address, not because SAP asserts two incompatible facts.

contradictions.topic: How many options the Rules-tab Tolerance control offers, whether Currency is one of them, and whether the second option carries the '(+/-)' suffix.

readings.summary: step-3 introduces the control as a single choice and then enumerates FOUR options as its own bullet run — None, Within (+/-), Custom, Currency — each with its own definition.
readings.sourceQuote: Choose one tolerance:

readings.summary: step-3's second bullet carries the '(+/-)' suffix on the Within option.
readings.sourceQuote: Within (+/-): Choose this to specify a balanced amount of tolerance equal above and below that of the PO field being matched to the same request field

readings.summary: step-3's fourth bullet presents Currency as a peer tolerance choice, defined as a base-currency selection.
readings.sourceQuote: Currency: Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system. This functions as for other rule sets, including audit rules.
